list.title: module:CurrentSubtitleRow.BADGE_ICON_NONE
list.description: Which icon a badge draws. Both Posters live in every slot with their uri assigned once — see SubtitleResultRow.buildBadgePool for the full reasoning.

list.title: module:CurrentSubtitleRow.BADGE_POOL_SIZE
list.description: Badge slots pre-allocated per row, sized to the most badges a single row of this type can carry so the pool never grows mid-scroll.

list.title: module:CurrentSubtitleRow.badgesFor
list.description:
badgesFor: Only the flags that change what the track IS, most significant first.

Order is load-bearing: when a row cannot fit every badge, the ones dropped are the last in this list (see placeBadges).

No "perfect match" here — that is a property of a provider search result, not of a file already on disk — and no download count, which an installed subtitle does not have. Rendering those was what made the first draft's right-hand column read as broken.

list.title: module:CurrentSubtitleRow.buildBadgePool
list.description:
buildBadgePool: Create the badge nodes ONCE.

MarkupList recycles a small set of row components as the list scrolls, writing a new itemContent into each. The first draft tore down and rebuilt every badge child on each of those writes, so a single scroll step cost a burst of node create/destroy per visible row -- which is what made scrolling feel heavy. Nodes are now created once; only their text, colour and visibility change.

list.title: module:CurrentSubtitleRow.fillBadgeSlot
list.description: fillBadgeSlot: Draw one badge in a slot. Chooses WHICH resident icon shows; never assigns a uri, which is what keeps a recycled row from rebinding a texture.

list.title: module:CurrentSubtitleRow.newBadge
list.description: newBadge: A wanted badge with its rendered width, measured once per content.

list.title: module:CurrentSubtitleRow.newBadgeIcon
list.description: newBadgeIcon: one resident, pre-bound badge Poster, collapsed until used. Starts at zero WIDTH rather than merely hidden — an invisible LayoutGroup child still takes its place in the layout, which is what leaves a badge with no icon indented from one that has it.

list.title: module:CurrentSubtitleRow.placeBadges
list.description:
placeBadges: Show as many wanted badges as the row allows, right-aligned.

Filled into the LAST slots of the pool, in order, and the unused slots are hidden. badgeRow is right-aligned, so the last slot sits on the row's right edge; a hidden slot still takes its place in a LayoutGroup, so leaving the unused ones at the FRONT keeps them out of the way instead of pushing the visible badges in from the edge.

list.title: module:CurrentSubtitleRow.titleLineFor
list.description:
titleLineFor: "English · SRT".

Language first because that is what this column is scanned for. The codec follows because it is the one remaining property that changes how the track behaves (an image-based format forces transcoding where a text one does not).

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.EXTRAS_BOTTOM_SAFE_PADDING
list.description: Extra clearance so the focused row's bottom edge sits comfortably above the 5% action-safe zone. Adjusting this shifts BOTTOM and MIDDLE positions equally relative to the action zone.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.EXTRAS_ROWLIST_DEFAULT_Y
list.description: Default RowList translation.y — places the focused row (TOP) 18px below the panel top edge.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.applyRowLayout
list.description:
applyRowLayout: Write the layout for the rows on screen in one setFields.

numRows must always equal the actual row count so floatingFocus never needs to scroll: if numRows < rowCount, navigation scrolls internally, which moves the focused row's RowList Y unpredictably and breaks updatePanelPosition's translation formula.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.cancelRun
list.description: cancelRun: Drop the run in flight, if any. Its Task node is released with it, so nothing it delivers later can reach onExtrasRowReady, which only ever drains the current node.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.commitRows
list.description:
commitRows: Bring the rows on screen in line with the run's results in one pass — and write NOTHING that has not changed, because every write to an on-screen row redraws the counter (see startRun).

  • A row whose title, slot shape and source-content digest match what is on screen is left untouched (extrasRows.isRowUnchanged).
  • A changed row that is already on screen is reused so focus position survives; its new items are appended BEFORE the old ones are removed, so it is never momentarily empty (the same rule HomeRows.populateRowFromData follows).
  • A row whose fetch failed is KEPT: no answer says nothing about what the item has, and removing it would delete good content on a flaky refresh. See extrasRows.rowDisposition.
  • The layout is written only when a row was added, removed or re-shaped.

Which of those applies to each row is decided by extrasRows.commitActions, which is unit-tested; this applies its answer to the nodes.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.fillRow
list.description: fillRow: The row node for kind, holding result.items — the row already on screen when there is one, a new node otherwise.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.finishRunIfResolved
list.description: finishRunIfResolved: Once every slot of the run has resolved, commit and close the run.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.loadParts
list.description: loadParts: Load the extras rows for an item. m.top.type must be set first (ItemDetails does). Rows per type are decided by extrasRows.plan; the server version decides whether a Collections row is one of them.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.onDestroy
list.description: onDestroy: Full teardown releasing all resources before component removal. Called by ItemDetails.onDestroy() before nulling the extrasGrid reference.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.onExtrasRowReady
list.description: onExtrasRowReady: Drain every result the orchestrator has appended since the last wake — wake events coalesce, appended children don't.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.onKeyEvent
list.description: onKeyEvent: Anticipate the next row on UP/DOWN so the panel translation animation starts in sync with the RowList floatingFocus animation rather than after it completes. Returns false so the RowList handles the actual navigation.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.onProgramsExpired
list.description:
Fires when JRRowList's progress tick detects at least one expired Program among this list's rows. Refetches ONLY the Channel Programs row (TvChannel "Up Next" / Program "More on this Channel") so finished broadcasts roll off — related content is stable over a viewing session and is not refetched.

Skipped while any run is in flight: starting a run cancels the one in progress, which would throw away its other rows. The tick raises the flag again on its next pass while a program is still expired, so nothing is lost by waiting.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.resetForLoad
list.description: resetForLoad: State a full load starts from. A targeted refetch (onProgramsExpired) skips this — it must not move the panel or reopen the readiness signal.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.resolveSlot
list.description: resolveSlot: Record one row's outcome for the commit.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.setPlan
list.description: setPlan: Adopt a plan, stamping each row with slot, its index — the key results come back on.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.startRun
list.description:
startRun: Load runRows (all of m.plan, or a subset of it for a targeted refetch).

Nothing reaches the RowList until the WHOLE run has resolved; then commitRows applies every change in one pass. That is the point of this component's shape, not an incidental: RowList redraws its "X of Y" row counter on any write to rows already on screen — a row appended below them, a live row's items replaced — even when the count it shows does not change, and that redraw read as a flicker. Measured on device: committing rows as each resolved blinked once per commit after the first, and one commit that rewrote unchanged rows still blinked once.

list.title: module:ExtrasRowList.updatePanelPosition
list.description:
updatePanelPosition: Set targetTranslationY so ItemDetails.bs can animate the RowList's translation within extrasGrp. extrasGrp stays fixed at extrasLayout.PANEL_OPEN_Y (306).

numRows always equals the total row count (set in applyRowLayout), so floatingFocus never scrolls internally. All rows stay at fixed RowList-relative Y positions: row 0 → RowList Y = 0 row N → RowList Y = sum(heights[0..N-1]) + N * m.rowSpacing (= focusedRowY)

Visible screen height between panel top and action zone: extrasLayout.ACTION_SAFE_BOTTOM_Y - extrasLayout.PANEL_OPEN_Y = 720px.

Three position classes: TOP — row 0 (or only row): focused row at RowList Y=0, default translation (18px). BOTTOM — last row: focused row bottom edge at action zone - EXTRAS_BOTTOM_SAFE_PADDING. extrasLayout.PANEL_OPEN_Y + translationY + focusedRowY + rowHeight = extrasLayout.ACTION_SAFE_BOTTOM_Y - EXTRAS_BOTTOM_SAFE_PADDING translationY = (extrasLayout.ACTION_SAFE_BOTTOM_Y - extrasLayout.PANEL_OPEN_Y - EXTRAS_BOTTOM_SAFE_PADDING) - rowHeight - focusedRowY MIDDLE — rows 1..N-2: focused row centered in the visible area. translationY = int((extrasLayout.ACTION_SAFE_BOTTOM_Y - extrasLayout.PANEL_OPEN_Y - rowHeight) / 2) - focusedRowY

Negative translationY moves the RowList above extrasGrp Y=0. The clippingRect Group in ExtrasSlider.xml clips that overflow so the previous row only peeks within the panel bounds. targetTranslationY is observed by ItemDetails.bs which runs the gridAnime Animation. Called early from onKeyEvent (before RowList focuses the row) and confirmed by onRowItemFocused.

list.title: module:FocusableOverview.openOverviewDialog
list.description:
Opens an OverviewDialog as a full-screen overlay on the scene, through the standard helper. Tagline goes separately so the dialog can style it distinctly.

This used to hand-roll the append (createObject + appendChild + setFocus). The helper does the same thing AND stamps the shared overlay id, which is what isOverlayDialogOpen / isDialogOpen / cancelOpenDialog find an open dialog by — so the hand-rolled version was invisible to all three, and OverviewDialog's own cancelDialog() was unreachable on this path.

We pass returnFocusTo explicitly rather than letting the helper derive it: the opener is us, we know it, and a derived answer is only incidentally the same node.

list.title: module:GetPlaybackInfoTask.getPlaybackInfoTask
list.description:
Fetch this device's live session. That is ALL this task does.

It used to build the whole report here — reading user settings, choosing labels, calling translate() — which was the wrong split three times over. The work is pure computation that needed no Task thread; every m.global read it made cost ~93 µs from here against ~2 µs from the render thread; and the built report was then cached for the life of the player, so a DoVi buffer-overflow fallback (transcode -> direct play) left the "i" button still reporting a transcode that had stopped.

Now the network call is the only thing on this thread and PlayerHostView composes the report per press from this plus the cached PlaybackInfo. Rebuilding is cheap enough to do every time, which is what makes the report honest about a stream that changed underneath it.

session is left invalid when the server returns nothing — that is a real state (the server has not registered playback yet), and the renderer says so rather than the task inventing an error section.

list.title: module:GridItem.evaluateGridTextureState
list.description:
Central texture decision — called when renderTracking, textureManagerState, or loadedRowRange changes.

State machine (same as JRRowItem but without horizontal buffer): "destroyed" → force unload everything (no guards) "init" → no-op (freeze state during layout changes) "hidden" → no-op (freeze — screen is behind another on the stack) "active" → managed rows (visible + buffer): always loaded. Outside rows: renderTracking decides.

list.title: module:GridItem.forceUnloadGridTexture
list.description: Force-unloads textures unconditionally — used only during onDestroy(). Ignores m.isTextureUnloaded and m.cachedPosterUri guards so every cell releases memory.

list.title: module:GridItem.getGridRowPosition
list.description: Returns this cell's row position relative to the managed row ranges. Derives the grid row from the cached flat index and numColumns. or "outside" if not in any managed range

list.title: module:GridItem.getGridTextureManagerState
list.description: Returns the current texture manager state from the content root.

list.title: module:GridItem.isRepeatBind

list.title: module:GridItem.noteAppearance
list.description: Mirror of JRRowItem.noteAppearance — same pop-in question, same two call sites, same reason for using renderTracking rather than getGridRowPosition(). See that function for the full rationale; the grid keeps its own copy because the two cell components are parallel by design and share no base.

list.title: module:GridItem.onFocusChanged
list.description: Enable title scrolling based on item focus

list.title: module:GridItem.onItemContentChanged
list.description: Re-render when the parent assigns a new item to this (possibly recycled) cell. Texture observers only need itemContent, so wire them up even before the cell has been sized; the actual render waits until width/height are known (onSizeChanged fires the first paint when the parent applies itemSize/rowItemSize).

list.title: module:GridItem.onLoadedRowRangeChanged
list.description: Fires when the parent screen updates the loaded row range (focus change).

list.title: module:GridItem.onPosterLoadStatusChanged
list.description: Toggle the JRPlaceholder fallback based on the real poster's load state. Mirrors the canonical state machine from JRRowItem.bs onPosterLoadStatusChanged.

list.title: module:GridItem.onRenderTrackingChanged
list.description: Fires when the cell scrolls in/out of the visible area.

list.title: module:GridItem.onSizeChanged
