list.description: removeResumeButtonWithFocus: Remove resume button while preserving focus position

list.title: module:ItemDetails.removeResumeLoadingButton
list.description: removeResumeLoadingButton: Remove the resume LoadingButton placeholder if still present. Called when async data confirms no resume episode exists (nextUpEpisode stays invalid).

list.title: module:ItemDetails.requestLogoSize
list.description: The size the server will send the logo at, from the original size it reports, drawn through the same logoBoxFor() the loaded bitmap uses. No answer, or a size of 0 (the server has none recorded), leaves the text waiting on the image itself.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.requestMostRecentVersion
list.description:
requestMostRecentVersion: Ask the server which version it would resume, once per content load.

The source order answers that only from a primary; this screen can be showing an alternate (see versionResume.chooseResumeSource). Scoped to the item's parent and lean, as in LoadVideoContentTask.fetchMostRecentVersionId, so both shells ask the same question.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.requestServerResumePolicy
list.description:
requestServerResumePolicy: Read GET /System/Configuration the first time a carry needs it.

Fails CLOSED: while the thresholds are unknown wouldMarkPlayed() answers "played", so nothing is carried — a carried position past a threshold would mark the item played and erase the place being resumed from. A failed read is remembered only for this content load, not on the server node, so the next one asks again.

failed for this content load, or its request could not be built

list.title: module:ItemDetails.requestVersionPosition
list.description:
requestVersionPosition: Fetch one version's own position, once per content load.

built, in which case the position is already recorded as unreadable

list.title: module:ItemDetails.resetInfoRows
list.description: Empty all three info rows before a rebuild.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.resetVersionResume
list.description: resetVersionResume: Start per-version resume state for newly loaded content. Leaves m.versionResume invalid — "use the item's own position", as before 12.0 — unless the server keeps positions per version and the item has alternate versions.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.resolveGoToArtistId
list.description: Resolve the artist id for goToArtist: prefer the primary album artist, fall back to the single artist item.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.resolveResumeState
list.description: resolveResumeState: Where Resume starts for the selected version, starting any fetch that answer still needs.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.resumeSeriesNextUp
list.description: Series Resume plays the next-up episode (a single item) from its saved position, via the play route.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.rowHeight
list.description: A row's height before layout: its tallest child for a horizontal group, else its own.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.selectedMediaSource
list.description: selectedMediaSource: The currently selected MediaSource AA, or invalid. Uses the same resolution as the track dropdowns (findSelectedSource), so the panel and the dropdowns can never disagree about which version is in play.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.seriesResumeLoadingText
list.description: seriesResumeLoadingText: The Series placeholder label — the episode-specific text (e.g. "Resume S2E3") from prior data when there is some, so the label holds steady through a reload, otherwise plain "Resume".

list.title: module:ItemDetails.serverResumePolicy
list.description: serverResumePolicy: The server's resume thresholds, if they have been read.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.setDateAdded
list.description: setDateAdded: Set date added label text and position at bottom right corner

list.title: module:ItemDetails.setDescriptionInLayout
list.description: setDescriptionInLayout: Add or remove itemDescription from the itemDetails LayoutGroup. Invisible nodes still take up space in RSG LayoutGroups, so reparenting is required to truly eliminate spacing when there is no description text.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.setItemLogo
list.description:
setItemLogo: Set the item logo image URL if available. Fallback chains by type — every chain ends in a typed placeholder via getPlaceholderImagePath() so the logo slot never goes blank, matching the pattern Person and MusicArtist always used:

  • Movie/Series/BoxSet: Logo → primaryImageTag (poster, compact size) → placeholder
  • Episode/Season/Recording: primaryImageTag → parentLogoImageTag (series logo) → seriesPrimaryImageTag → placeholder
  • Video/MusicVideo: primaryImageTag → placeholder
  • MusicAlbum / Playlist / Photo / PhotoAlbum / TvChannel: primaryImageTag → placeholder
  • Program: primaryImageTag → channel logo → placeholder
  • Audio: primaryImageTag → album art → placeholder
  • Person / MusicArtist: primaryImageTag (portrait) → placeholder

list.title: module:ItemDetails.setLogoBox
list.description: The logo's place on screen is known: newBox, or invalid for no logo at all.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.setLogoImage
list.description: Point the logo at a server image, and ask the server for the image's size so the text can be fitted before the image itself arrives. A first request for a resized image can take seconds while the server makes it (measured 2026-09-22: 0.26 s median, 3 s worst, on a LAN); the size answers in tens of milliseconds.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.setLogoPlaceholder
list.description: Point the logo at a packaged placeholder. It loads in moments, and its size is learned when it does (onLogoLoadStatusChanged).

list.title: module:ItemDetails.setTracksInLayout
list.description: setTracksInLayout: Add or remove the 62px itemTracks spacer from the itemDetails LayoutGroup. When a track cluster is applicable to the current item, the spacer stays in the layout and pushes description bottom up to y=701 so the trackCluster sibling can sit at y=713 with 12px breathing pad above and 18px below between the description and the button group. For item types without any media tracks (Series/Person/etc.), the spacer is removed and description bottom drops back to y=775 (matching main's behavior — no cluster, no padding, no regression).

list.title: module:ItemDetails.setupButtons
list.description: setupButtons: Build the complete button set for the given item type. Clears all existing buttons and adds the correct sync buttons in order. Loading placeholders are added for async buttons (Series Resume, Person Shuffle) so the button row renders at its final width immediately. The async handlers replace or remove the placeholders when data arrives. Called on every itemContentChanged — the button list is rebuilt from scratch each time.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.startPlayFromDetail
list.description: Build the single-item play queue from this detail's own state and navigate to the play route. The router is idle (the user pressed a button on this settled view), so navigateTo won't hit the in-progress guard, and the PlayerHostView reads this queue on mount.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.swapResumeLoadingButton
list.description: swapResumeLoadingButton: Replace the loading placeholder with the real Resume button at the same index. The user may have moved focus while the data loaded; removing and then inserting at one index is a net-zero shift, so the focus index read first still names the same button. Real focus moves only if the placeholder itself had it.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.syncVersionSelectionToChoice
list.description:
syncVersionSelectionToChoice: Move the selected version to the one that should resume, once enough positions are known to say which that is.

The details screen's first guess is made before any position has been read — it can only go on the server's source order. That order names the most recently played version, which is the rule's usual answer, but not when two versions sit at about the same place: there the better version for the device wins, and deciding that needs their actual positions. So the choice is re-run as each position lands, and the SAME pure function answers it here as in LoadVideoContentTask, which is what keeps the screen from naming one version while quick play, a cast or Continue Watching plays another.

Requests ride the existing per-version fetch, so a position already read or in flight is not asked for twice, and each reply re-enters here through onVersionPositionLoaded.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.toggleFavorite
list.description: callFunc entry — toggles the favorite state of the current item. Invoked from main.bs's button router; because callFunc rendezvouses to this render-thread-owned node, the body (and the fetchAsync().then() promise delivery + auto-abandon) runs on this component's render thread, where the named-observer adapter works. This is the Phase-3c canonical "main thread → render thread delegation" pattern — see docs/dev/promises.md. It moves the favorite toggle off main.bs's god-loop (was submitApiRequest + isDone branch + handler).

list.title: module:ItemDetails.toggleWatched
list.description: callFunc entry — toggles the watched/played state of the current item. Invoked from main.bs's button router; Movie/Episode call it directly, while Series route through the "mark all episodes" confirmation dialog first (main.bs keeps that dialog routing and re-invokes this on confirm — #550 sgRouter territory). Because callFunc rendezvouses to this render-thread-owned node, the body (and the fetchAsync().then() promise delivery + auto-abandon) runs on this component's render thread, where the named-observer adapter works. This is the deferred twin of toggleFavorite() — the Phase-3c "main thread → render thread delegation" pattern (see docs/dev/promises.md). It moves the LAST raw submitApiRequest + isDone flow off main.bs's god-loop.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.trackVersionResumeFill
list.description:
trackVersionResumeFill: Declare the Resume slot's loading state to the readiness ledger.

A Movie's Resume button is otherwise built synchronously from the item, but on a per-version server it can wait on a version's position or the server's thresholds, and settled must not fire while it does. Declared on the first loading answer and resolved on the first final one; the flag lives on m, not on m.versionResume, so a content reload that drops that state cannot orphan the declaration. After the screen has settled (a version switch, a refresh) the ledger ignores both sides.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.triggerTextForSelection
list.description: triggerTextForSelection: Look up the currently-selected item's display title. Prefers triggerTitle where an item carries one — the video and subtitle slots use it to keep the collapsed trigger free of what only reads correctly beside the other entries. Audio items have no triggerTitle and fall through to title unchanged.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.unsplitButtons
list.description:
The two halves of the contract. Both delegate to source/utils/buttonOverflow.bs so the OSD's row runs the same implementation rather than a second copy of it; what stays here is only which nodes this screen's row is made of.

The closing half puts focus back on the button that had it when the opening half ran. A mutator that moves focus to a DIFFERENT button on purpose (a new Resume taking over from Play) must say so with claimRowFocus(m.buttonOverflow, id) between the two, or its choice is silently reverted — see ItemDetailsRowFocus.spec.bs.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.updateItemDetailsAnimationTarget
list.description: updateItemDetailsAnimationTarget: Slide itemDetails so the bottom of itemInfoRows sits just above the extras pane. boundingRect() on a child returns LOCAL coords relative to the parent's translation point, so we use translation[1] (not boundingRect().y) as the screen origin. Called just-in-time from the DOWN key handler to guarantee the layout is fully settled (text wrapping complete) before measuring. Eager calculation via renderTracking races with async text layout, producing stale targets — especially for long descriptions.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.updatePersonShuffle
list.description:
updatePersonShuffle: Bring the Person row's Shuffle slot in line with the media chain. Shows Shuffle when the chain has found media — replacing the setupButtons() placeholder, or inserting before Favorite when there is none. Removes the placeholder, or a Shuffle whose media has gone, only on the chain's FINAL answer.

personHasMedia means "no media"; false when that false may be a run's reset

list.title: module:ItemDetails.updatePlaylistItemCountLabel
list.description: The Playlist info row's count: "Tracks" only when the playlist is positively confirmed all-audio. "unknown" (load failure) and "mixed" both fall through to "Items" — the safe neutral default.

list.title: module:ItemDetails.zeroVersionPositions
list.description: zeroVersionPositions: A positions map recording that no version has a position.

list.description: Switch menu shown when button focus changes

list.title: module:ItemGridOptions.isFilterMenuDataValid
list.description: Check if data for Filter Menu is valid

list.title: module:JRButtonGroup.center
list.description: center the button group horizontally NOTE: this centers using the entire screen width, not the parent bounding rect

list.title: module:JRButtonGroup.doCentering
list.description: Actually perform the centering calculation

list.title: module:JRButtonGroup.onChildReady
list.description: Called when a child button becomes ready

list.title: module:JRButtons.BUTTON_FONT_SIZE
list.description: TextSizeTask measures at this size and showButtons renders at it. They must agree or the labels are laid out to the wrong widths, so it is one constant rather than two literals.

list.title: module:JRButtons.cancelTextSizeTask
list.description: Stop, unobserve, and drop the in-flight TextSizeTask if one exists. Safe to call when none is active. The single teardown path for m.textSizeTask, mirroring QueueManager's cancelActive*. JRButtons extends Group, so no onDestroy lifecycle hook runs on it — releasing the node as soon as its one-shot measurement lands is what keeps it from outliving the screen.

list.title: module:JRButtons.focusChanged
list.description: Change opacity of the highlighted menu item based on focus

list.title: module:JRButtons.highlightSelected
list.description: Highlight selected menu option

list.title: module:JRButtons.onSelectedIndexChanged
list.description: When Selected Index set, ensure it is the one Focused

list.title: module:JRButtons.renderChanged
list.description: When options are fully displayed, set focus and selected option

list.title: module:JRButtons.showButtons
list.description: Rebuilds the label row. Clears first so a second buttons write replaces the row instead of appending a second copy of it — createChild appends, and buttonCount drives key nav.

list.title: module:JRButtons.updateButtons
list.description: buttons onChange. The measurement has to happen on a Task: it needs roFontRegistry, which Roku refuses to create on the render thread ("MAIN|TASK-only component"). The task is built per write and released in showButtons, so nothing is retained between measurements.

list.title: module:JRDialog.BUTTON_SPACING
list.description:
Layout is DERIVED, not a stack of fixed offsets: every block is measured and the next one flows below it. Fixed offsets could not survive a title that wraps to two lines, a message of any length, or a button row whose width depends on the translation.

The flow itself — the order of the blocks and the gaps between them — lives in source/utils/dialogLayout.bs, shared with JRListDialog and OverviewDialog and unit-tested there. What stays here is what is specific to THIS dialog: a panel that grows to fit its button row, and the row that made it grow.

list.title: module:JRDialog.OPENING_ANNOUNCEMENT_DELAY
list.description:
The ONE piece of narration timing that cannot be event-driven.

Established on-device, one behavior at a time:

  • The platform announces the focused button ONLY when focus first enters the dialog. Moving between buttons afterwards is silent (TextButton extends Group, not Roku's Button, so the "text of button is spoken only if focused" rule never applies). Those moves are ours alone, and need no timing.
  • That one initial announcement FLUSHES ours. Speaking from the focus observer, which is as early as any event lets us react, still loses: the platform speaks after us and we are cut off. Speaking before focus loses the same way. To survive we must speak AFTER the platform's announcement, and SceneGraph exposes no event for "the platform has finished dispatching speech" — the only observable speech events are for utterances the app itself starts. So the opening announcement is the one place a delay is unavoidable.

Keep it short: long enough to land second, short enough to flush the platform's word before it is audible. At 0.6s the clipped word was clearly audible. Changing this needs an ear, not reasoning — there is no test that can catch it.

list.title: module:JRDialog.PANEL_WIDTH
list.description:
Width starts here and GROWS to fit the button row (long translations), up to PANEL_MAX_WIDTH. Past that the row stacks vertically instead of overflowing.

Both on the 6px scale so the panel's left and right edges land on the 720p output grid: (1920 - w) / 2 = 960 - w/2, so a width divisible by 6 gives a panelX divisible by 3. 760 did not, which put both vertical edges off it.

list.title: module:JRDialog.applyButtonLayout
list.description: Horizontal row normally; vertical, full-width buttons when they cannot fit.

list.title: module:JRDialog.applyLayout
list.description:
Position the chrome. Called on any content change; safe to run repeatedly.

Everything is measured then flowed, so a two-line title, a long message and a wide button row each push what follows instead of colliding with it.

list.title: module:JRDialog.buttonRowHeight
list.description: Rendered height of the button row, or a computed fallback before it lays out (localBoundingRect is 0 until the TextButtons size themselves).

list.title: module:JRDialog.cancelDialog
list.description:
Cancel this dialog from OUTSIDE — see cancelOpenDialog() in source/utils/dialogs.bs. Routed through resolveDialog so the once-only guard and the standard cancelled result both apply: a third party clearing the screen must be indistinguishable from the user pressing Back, or the owner waiting on the result is stranded.

Indistinguishable in what it DELIVERS, not in where it came from — the result also carries externallyCancelled, so an owner whose handler ACTS can decline to act on a close the user did not make. Everyone else reads cancelled and is unaffected. See source/utils/dialogResult.bs.

list.title: module:JRDialog.centerButtonRow
list.description: Centre the row on the PANEL, not the screen — they only coincided while the panel was a fixed width centred on screen.

list.title: module:JRDialog.closeDialog
list.description: Dismiss this overlay. Appended directly to the scene by dialogs.bs, so closing is a removeChild from our parent + restoring focus to the opener (returnFocusTo). Mirrors OverviewDialog.closeDialog().

list.title: module:JRDialog.moveButtonFocus
list.description:
Step button focus, WRAPPING at the ends to match JRButtonGroup — the app's other horizontal button row wraps, so a dialog that dead-ends feels broken.

Narration of the newly focused button is handled by the focusedChild observer, so it covers remote-driven moves and programmatic ones alike.

list.title: module:JRDialog.naturalButtonRowWidth
list.description: Width the row wants at its natural size, before any panel growth.

list.title: module:JRDialog.onButtonFocusChanged
list.description:
Screen-reader announcement, driven by the focus event itself.

The platform announces the focused button the moment focus lands, and app speech and platform speech interrupt each other rather than queueing — so we have to speak second to be the one that survives. The focus change IS that moment, so reacting to it needs no guess about timing (an earlier version used a tuned delay; the value was a guess that would rot on different hardware).

First focus = the dialog opening: announce the whole thing, folding in the button so it is one utterance in the built-in order. Later focus changes announce just the button the user moved to — nothing else has changed.

list.title: module:JRDialog.onButtonReady
list.description: A button finished sizing itself. Re-run the whole layout, not just the centring: the panel's width and height and the row's position are all derived from the buttons' real measurements. Laying out once from an estimate left the bottom padding short, and left a stacked row positioned off the panel.

list.title: module:JRDialog.onKeyEvent
list.description: The decision itself is buttonDialogKeyAction in source/utils/dialogKeys.bs, which is pure and unit-tested. Everything here is the doing.

list.title: module:JRDialog.onOpeningAnnouncementDue
list.description: Announce the whole dialog, once the platform's own focus announcement is out of the way. Folds in the focused button so this is a single utterance in the built-in order: title, message, button.

list.title: module:JRDialog.onSubheadingChanged
list.description: SET THE TEXT FIELDS BEFORE PRESENTING, never after. renderTracking fires on the none -> full transition and never again (the same property that made the button row use TextButton's isReady instead), so once the dialog has rendered no later text change re-runs applyLayout — the new text draws on top of the old layout. True of title and message too; the helpers in source/utils/dialogs.bs set every field before presentOverlayDialog for exactly this reason.

list.title: module:JRDialog.resolveDialog
list.description: Resolve the dialog exactly once, then close. index = -1 means cancelled (back). externallyCancelled is true only on the cancelDialog() path below.

list.title: module:JRDialog.settleLayout
list.description:
Lay out NOW, called by presentOverlayDialog once this dialog is attached.

The dialog is hidden until this returns, so there is no renderTracking to wait on — and none is needed, because localBoundingRect() answers while hidden. See dialogReveal.bs.

list.title: module:JRDialogPanel.onLayoutChanged
list.description: Position the chrome from a computed layout. Pure rendering: if a rect looks wrong, the bug is in computeDialogLayout (which is unit-tested) or in what the caller measured, not here.

list.title: module:JRDialogPanel.onTitleRendered
list.description: renderTracking fires once the new text has laid out, which is when a height first exists to read.

list.title: module:JRGroup.onDestroy
list.description:
Base codebehind for JRGroup — the parent of every sub-panel / dialog (and, transitively, every JRScreen). Kept intentionally minimal: it exists only to provide the onDestroy() floor below.

Floor for JRGroup subclasses (panels/dialogs) that DON'T override onDestroy(): abandon any pending fetchAsync promises so a late pool response can't fire a callback into the destroyed node. Subclasses that DO override onDestroy() get this via the auto-abandon-promises BSC plugin (which injects abandonApiPromises() into their own onDestroy) — SG component onDestroy does not chain to this base, so the call can't rely on inheritance alone.

list.title: module:JRKeyboardDialog.onWasClosed

list.title: module:JRListDialogRow.CHECK_ICON_SIZE
list.description:
The gutter and padding live in dialogLayout.bs (LIST_ROW_CHECK_GUTTER / LIST_ROW_PADDING) so the spacing gate covers them.

CHECK_ICON_SIZE stays HERE and stays off the 6px scale on purpose: it is the source bitmap's size, not a spacing choice. The $$RES$$ pipeline substitutes a 23x23 _hd asset decoded at physical output size, so 35 design units is 1:1 on both tiers — rounding it to 36 would break that and soften the glyph.

list.title: module:JROverhang.onTabBarReady

list.description: Called when user dropdown signals LEFT or RIGHT exit

list.title: module:JROverhang.positionTabBar

When the clock is hidden, the dropdown is right-aligned so its right edge meets the 5% action-safe boundary (x=1824), matching where the clock's right edge sits.

list.description: Button size: matches dropdown trigger height

list.description: Toggle visual state between unfocused (transparent) and focused (backdrop + border)

list.title: module:JRPlaceholder.onItemTypeChanged
list.description: Empty itemType → loading state (backdrop visible, glyph hidden). Non-empty itemType → placeholder fallback state (backdrop + tinted glyph).

list.title: module:JRPlaceholder.onSizeChanged
list.description: Resize the backdrop and glyph to track the parent's declared dimensions. Glyph uses scaleToFit (declared in XML) so the 256×256 placeholder PNG renders centered at the smaller of width/height, preserving aspect ratio. setFields batches the two writes per child, halving the field-write count.

list.title: module:JRPoster.PROGRESS_BAR_STRIP
list.description: VideoProgressBar's own height — the strip the bar occupies along the poster's bottom edge.

list.title: module:JRPoster.VERSIONS_BADGE_GAP
list.description: Gap between the versions badge and the bar. Without it the badge's bottom edge IS the bar's top edge, and the two read as one welded element on a partly-watched tile.

list.title: module:JRPoster.onMediaSourceCountChanged
list.description:
Marks a tile whose item has more than one version, so the choice is visible while browsing instead of only on the details screen.

Pinned to the BOTTOM-LEFT, clear of the progress bar's strip plus a gap. The bar is added and removed on demand, so this badge cannot depend on whether it is there — the offset is computed from the constants, not from a bar node that may not exist yet.

Still flush to the LEFT edge, matching the watched badge's flush top-right anchoring. If the badge system later adopts a uniform inset, both move together — see poster-badge-system-undesigned.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.FOCUS_PADDING
list.description: Vertical gap between the bottom of the poster (= bottom of the RowList focus ring) and the first text label. Prevents the focus border from overlapping the title. The title stays OUTSIDE the focus border because the RowList sets rowHeights taller than rowItemSize — see docs/architecture/list-grid-item-layout.md.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.applyPlayedPercentage
list.description:
Sets the poster's progress bar percentage based on item type. Programs use live broadcast elapsed time (wall-clock derived); everything else uses UserData.PlayedPercentage as flattened by the data transformer.

For Programs, also installs a reactive bridge observer on the content node's playedPercentage field. JRRowList's 60s tick rewrites that field, and this observer forwards the change to m.poster.playedPercentage — updating any currently-mounted VideoProgressBar without a cell re-render.

Observer teardown is split across two sites to cover every itemContent transition this cell can see: • renderItem() top — handles transitions into a new valid bind (recycle into a different content node) and re-renders triggered by size changes on the same item. Required so applyPlayedPercentage doesn't double- install observers on size-change re-renders. • onItemContentChanged() invalid path — handles transitions to invalid, which never reach renderItem() and would otherwise leak the observer. This function therefore only needs to install — not clear.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.arrangeIconAndBackdropText
list.description: Centers the icon in the upper portion of the backdrop and positions the library name label below it.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.deferTextureLoad
list.description:
Skips the image request for a cell the texture manager is keeping off screen. The caller has already cached the URI, so reloadTexture() issues the load when the cell enters the buffer zone.

Clearing the poster URI is what makes isTextureUnloaded true by construction. Leave a recycled cell's PREVIOUS poster live and the flag claims a texture was released while it is still resident: unloadTexture() then early-returns on that flag and never frees it, and the stale image can surface under the new item if the cell draws before its range observer fires. GridItem's equivalent branch clears it for the same reason.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.evaluateTextureState
list.description:
Central texture decision — called when renderTracking, textureManagerState, loadedRowRange, or focusedColumns changes.

State machine: "destroyed" → force unload everything (no guards) "init" → no-op (freeze state during layout changes) "hidden" → renderTracking decides (keep Roku-allocated cells, unload rest) "active" → managed rows (visible + buffer): our buffer logic decides, renderTracking ignored (it's unreliable during layout recalcs). Outside rows: renderTracking decides.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.forceUnloadTexture
list.description: Force-unloads textures unconditionally — used only during onDestroy(). Ignores m.isTextureUnloaded and m.cachedPosterUri guards so every cell releases memory.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.getLibraryIconPath
list.description: Maps a Jellyfin library collection type to a local icon image path. Used to display a type-appropriate icon on library tile backdrops.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.getMyColumnIndex
list.description: Returns this cell's column index (position within its row).

list.title: module:JRRowItem.getMyRowIndex
list.description: Returns this cell's row index by finding its row node in the content root's children. Computed on demand rather than cached because row indices shift when rows are dynamically inserted or removed (e.g. HomeRows section loading).

list.title: module:JRRowItem.getRowItemCount
list.description: Returns the number of items in this cell's row.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.getRowPosition
list.description: Returns this cell's position relative to the managed row ranges. or "outside" if not in any managed range

list.title: module:JRRowItem.getTextureManagerState
list.description: Returns the current texture manager state from the content root.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.hideLoadingSpinner
list.description: Hides and stops the loading spinner if it exists.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.initBackdropText
list.description: Lazy-creates the backdrop text label for library tiles on first use. Deferred allocation avoids creating the node for non-library rows.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.isInHorizontalBuffer
list.description: Checks whether this cell is in the horizontal buffer zone for its row. Reads the node state; the geometry itself is isColumnInTextureWindow (textureManager.bs), where it is unit-tested. Only applies to rows with > TEXTURE_BUFFER_THRESHOLD items.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.isRepeatBind
list.description: True when this cell is being bound to the SAME item at the SAME size it already holds — a bind that cannot change a single pixel and exists only to be counted as waste. Kept on the cell because its own previous bind is free to remember here, where storing it on the shared content root would cost a node round trip per bind. Reads id rather than a title: a skeleton placeholder carries ONLY type, and anything that CASTS an absent field (getRowItemTitle returns item.name as String) is a &h18 crash on that path. A field read compared with isValid is safe on every item shape.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.logTextureAction
list.description: Returns a human-readable identifier for the current cell: "[RowTitle] ItemName" Used in texture management logs so you can tell which item changed without decoding URLs. Uses m.log to avoid string concat crashes from invalid/non-string field values.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.noteAppearance
list.description:
Records that this cell is on screen, for the pop-in half of the cell-load ledger.

Called from BOTH renderItem (the cell was bound while already on screen — Home's first paint) and onRenderTrackingChanged (it scrolled in), because for a recycled cell there is no ordering guarantee between the two. cellLoad.appeared() counts at most once per bind, so calling it from both is idempotent rather than double-counting.

renderTracking is the appearance signal rather than getRowPosition() + isInHorizontalBuffer(), deliberately. Those are the app's own model of what is on screen, and the horizontal half assumes the focused column is the LEFTMOST visible one — an assumption this file's buffer maths makes and that has never been verified. Scoring the buffer against its own coordinate system would bake that unverified premise into the number; renderTracking is the compositor's answer and carries no such premise.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.onFocusChanged
list.description: Toggles scrolling vs static title on focus, and speaks the title via audio guide.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.onFocusedColumnsChanged
list.description: Fires when the parent screen updates the per-row focused column (horizontal scroll).

list.title: module:JRRowItem.onIconLoadStatusChanged
list.description: Shows the icon and repositions it with the backdrop text once the icon image loads. Hides the icon on failure so a stale image from a previous render does not persist.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.onLoadedRowRangeChanged
list.description: Fires when the parent screen updates the loaded row range (focus change).

list.title: module:JRRowItem.onPosterLoadStatusChanged
list.description:
Hides the placeholder (and any backdropText) once the real poster image loads. Shows the placeholder when the image is unavailable, still loading, or failed. On failure, sets placeholder.itemType so JRPlaceholder surfaces a type-appropriate glyph on the themed backdrop.

backdropText visibility is only toggled for library tiles — standard items must not inherit a stale label when this component instance is recycled from a library row.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.onProgramProgressChanged
list.description: Forwarded write from the bound Program content node to the live poster. Fires when JRRowList's tick rewrites the node's playedPercentage.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.onRenderTrackingChanged
list.description: Fires when the cell scrolls in/out of the visible area.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.onTextureManagerStateChanged
list.description: Fires when textureManagerState changes (init → active, active → hidden, etc.)

list.title: module:JRRowItem.reloadTexture
list.description:
Restores poster/icon URIs from cache when the cell scrolls back on screen. The placeholder will show briefly while the real image reloads from Roku's HTTP cache.

It is NOT a general retry path for a failed load. shouldReloadTexture deliberately skips a cell that is showing its failure glyph but was never unloaded — see failed-poster-no-scroll-retry in docs/decisions.md. Such a cell does get one fresh attempt, but only after it leaves the loaded range and unloadTexture sets the flag.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.renderLibraryTile
list.description: Renders a My Media library tile: themed backdrop + type icon + library name. The poster loads the library's Primary image; when it loads successfully the placeholder (and overlaid text) hide to reveal the image. Library tiles never set placeholder.itemType — the type-specific itemIcon (live_tv_white etc.) overlays the backdrop, so the JRPlaceholder glyph stays empty.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.renderStandardItem
list.description: Renders a standard item: poster image with title/subtitle text below.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.setupTextureObserver
list.description: One-time setup: observes loadedRowRange and focusedColumns on the RowList's content root. The content root is the grandparent of itemContent in the content tree: contentRoot → rowNode → itemNode (itemContent) Called from onItemContentChanged. Skips if already connected.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.shouldLoadTexture
list.description:
Determines whether this cell should load its texture during initial render. Used in renderStandardItem/renderLibraryTile to skip network requests for cells outside the buffer zone.

Determines whether this cell should load its poster during initial render. Mirrors evaluateTextureState logic: managed rows trust buffer logic, outside rows trust renderTracking.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.showLoadingSpinner
list.description: Shows the skeleton spinner over the backdrop for Loading placeholders. The sizing and placement live in source/utils/skeleton.bs so GridItem's skeleton cells draw the identical spinner rather than a second copy of it.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.showPlaceholder
list.description:
Shows a type-appropriate placeholder glyph on the themed backdrop. Delegated to JRPlaceholder, which owns the backdrop + glyph + themed-blendColor composition and the itemType → URI mapping (via getPlaceholderImagePath).

The poster URI is cleared to "" so a recycled cell's stale image (e.g., the previous cell's photo) doesn't render on top of the placeholder. JRPoster sits ON TOP of JRPlaceholder per the XML order, so a stale URI would cover the placeholder glyph entirely. m.cachedPosterUri retains the real URL so reloadTexture() can retry it when the cell scrolls back on screen.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.unloadTexture
list.description:
Clears poster/icon URIs to release texture memory when the cell is off-screen. Items with no real image (cachedPosterUri = "") are skipped — they already show a lightweight local placeholder that costs negligible texture memory.

cellLoad.UNLOAD_WINDOW. Required rather than defaulted: the two call sites below are the ONLY eviction paths, and a default would let a third one be added that silently scores as the wrong mechanism.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.unobserveProgramProgress
list.description: Tears down the bridge observer on the previously-bound Program content node. Called from two sites to cover every itemContent transition this cell sees: • Top of renderItem() — runs before tile/standard/loading branching so recycled cells never leak observers onto stale content nodes regardless of which render branch the new bind takes. Also covers size-change re- renders on the same item (without it, applyPlayedPercentage would stack duplicate observers on every size change). • Invalid path of onItemContentChanged() — covers transitions to invalid, which never reach renderItem(). Without this site, an observer installed on a Program node would leak when the cell unbinds.

list.title: module:JRRowItem.updateLayout
list.description: Updates positions and sizes of all child nodes to match the current slot dimensions. Called at the start of every renderItem() before branching into tile/standard mode.

list.title: module:JRRowList.init
list.description: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ FOCUS-INDICATOR LAYOUT CONTRACT — read before building/changing an item │ │ component (the itemComponentName) for any RowList. │ │ │ │ The focus indicator pins to the poster slot (rowItemSize) ONLY when │ │ rowHeights is set TALLER than the slot. Without rowHeights, it wraps the │ │ item component's full bounding box — including a title below the poster — so │ │ the border extends past the image and swallows the title. Set │ │ rowHeights = rowItemSize height + a title area, fill the poster at a top │ │ offset (so it overflows the slot and the border reads behind it), and put │ │ the title in the rowHeights area below. Canonical: JRRowItem + HomeRows. │ │ Full explanation + evidence: docs/architecture/list-grid-item-layout.md │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

list.title: module:JRRowList.onProgramProgressContentChanged
list.description: Fires when m.top.content is assigned or reassigned by a subclass. Rebinds the textureManagerState observer to the new content root so the tick timer tracks visibility transitions for the current data set.

list.title: module:JRRowList.onProgramProgressTick
list.description:
Walks the texture manager's loaded row range and rewrites playedPercentage on every Program child to its current broadcast-elapsed percentage. JRRowItem's bridge observer forwards these writes to any currently-mounted poster cells, refreshing visible bars without triggering a cell re-render. Non-Program items are skipped.

Iteration is scoped to loadedRowRange [bufferStart..bufferEnd] — the vertical range maintained by textureManager.bs — so large datasets (SearchRow, FavoritesRows) don't pay the cost of walking hundreds of offscreen items every minute on the render thread. Offscreen rows whose percentage goes stale during scroll-away will update at the next tick after re-entering the buffer range (up to ~60s stale window, accepted trade-off).

Also detects expired broadcasts (now >= PlayStart + PlayDuration) within the same buffer range and raises the programsExpired field. Subclasses that can refetch (HomeRows, ExtrasRowList) observe that field and trigger a fresh load. Expiry detection is scoped to the buffer range rather than the full content tree because Live TV rows in HomeRows/ExtrasRowList are always in the vertical buffer in practice — full-scan expiry on every tick would be unnecessary work for zero real-world benefit.

Hard-guards rather than full-scan fallback when loadedRowRange is missing or invalid: the tick only runs while textureManagerState = "active", which the state machine guarantees implies loadedRowRange is populated. A missing field surfaces an ordering regression loudly rather than masking it.

list.title: module:JRRowList.syncProgramProgressTicking
list.description: Starts or stops the 60s Program progress tick based on the visibility state broadcast by the texture manager. Idempotent; safe on every state change. State arrives as dynamic because textureManagerState is unset (invalid) on freshly-created content roots — setupTextureManager only assigns "init" after the subclass first populates the content tree.

list.title: module:JRScene.applyOverhangUserDropdown
list.description: Show the logged-in user in the overhang dropdown, or clear it to hide the dropdown. The name comes from the global user (the same value every post-login screen used to set imperatively), so a view only declares WHETHER the dropdown shows via shouldShowUserDropdown.

list.title: module:JRScene.cancelDeepLinkResolve
list.description: Abort an in-flight deep-link/cast resolve (the metadata fetch that runs BEFORE navigation): unobserve + stop + drop the task, clear its args, hide the spinner. Safe to call when none is pending. Reused by the back arbiter (a back during the resolve aborts the cast) and resetRouter (sign-out tears the resolve down with the router).

list.title: module:JRScene.initRouter
list.description:
Initialize the router (outlet + routes + observers) WITHOUT navigating. Idempotent: a no-op if a router already exists on the scene. Called lazily by routerNavigate (main thread) so the very first navigation — pre-login OR Home — brings the router up. Re-callable after resetRouter() (sign-out → re-login): sgRouter.initialize creates a fresh router when none exists on the scene.

The router hosts the FULL app — the pre-login flow (/server, /users, /login) as well as the post-login content/playback routes. The pre-login routes carry no canActivate guards (the redirect target /login is one of them); the post-login routes carry the AuthManager guard. Pre-login back transitions are coordinator-driven (loginRouter), not router-history-driven, because cold start can enter directly at /users with no /server in history.

list.title: module:JRScene.isRouterNavigating
list.description: Back-arbiter helper: is the router mid-navigation right now? Reads the public routerState field DIRECTLY (no observer). The routerState observer coalesces rapid writes and reliably drops the terminal NavigationEnd (proven on device), so a mirrored flag wedges true; a field READ never coalesces, so the field always holds the true latest state. A navigation runs through NavigationStart → … → NavigationEnd; any non-terminal type means a nav is in flight, a terminal type (or no router/state yet) means idle.

list.title: module:JRScene.navigateChainStep
list.description: Navigate routes[index], then chain to the next step once it settles (sgRouter's navigateTo promise resolves at NavigationEnd, so each .then() defers until the previous route is fully mounted). The final step takes remote focus. Context carries routes/index (BrightScript closures can't capture locals). clearLoginSpinnerOnEnd: threaded through to the FINAL step's navigateThenFocus so the login replay (replayRoutedDeepLink) keeps the blocking spinner up across the whole chain and clears it only once the last route mounts. The runtime-cast caller (replayDeepLinkReplacingPlayer) leaves it false — no login spinner is up there.

list.title: module:JRScene.navigateThenFocus
list.description: Navigate + take focus on settle + surface a rejected nav — the shared tail centralizing the navigate/focus/catch trio that was hand-copied across routerNavigate, navigateChainStep, and the settle drain (folds in finding A4: a rejected nav must re-assert focus, never strand the remote). routePath is dynamic: a string path for most calls, or a named-route AA ({ name, ... }) from routeForItem on the deep-link container path. sgRouter.navigateTo accepts both. clearSpinner: set by the login paths only. A blocking login spinner (started by the login coordinator on the OUTGOING pre-login view) is kept up across this async nav and cleared HERE, once the destination view has mounted (navigateTo resolves at NavigationEnd). Clearing it synchronously before the nav settles re-shows the outgoing pre-login view for a frame — the #677 login flash. Mirrors the ItemDetails -> player pattern (spinner stays up across the nav, the destination clears it).

list.title: module:JRScene.onActiveRoutedViewChanged
list.description: The router mounted (or switched to) a different content view. Re-point the overhang controller: tear down the binding to the previous view, bind the new one. (Lifted from SceneManager's register/unregister pair — same contract.)

list.title: module:JRScene.onExitConfirmResult
list.description: Exit prompt answered. exit is observed by main.bs on its message port; setting it returns from Main() and Roku OS tears the channel down.

list.title: module:JRScene.onIsLoadingChanged
list.description: Triggered when the isLoading boolean component field is changed

list.title: module:JRScene.onOverhangTabSelected
list.description: Proxy overhang tab selection back to the active routed view's selectedTabId.

list.title: module:JRScene.onPhotoLaunchRequested
list.description: A photo launcher (quickplay.photo / QueueManager slideshow output) signalled a photo-viewer launch. Carry the launch AA through as route context — PhotoDetails reads itemsNode/itemsArray + slideshow flags + start index from it on mount.

list.title: module:JRScene.onPlaybackLaunchRequested
list.description: QueueManager.playQueue signalled a video playback launch. The queue is already populated, so navigate to the play route — PlayerHostView mounts the player for the current queue item. :type/:id give the route a deep-link identity; the queue is the source of truth for what actually plays.

list.title: module:JRScene.onTestToast
list.description:
DEBUG: Triggered when testToast field is set from the BrightScript console. Format: "type|message" where type is "error", "success", "warning", or "info". Falls back to "error" type if no pipe delimiter is found.

Usage from BrightScript console (port 8085): m.top.getScene().testToast = "error|Something went wrong" m.top.getScene().testToast = "success|Item saved" m.top.getScene().testToast = "info|Loading filters..." m.top.getScene().testToast = "Just a message"

list.title: module:JRScene.refreshBackdropSetting
list.description: Re-evaluate and apply the backdrop visibility setting Useful when settings change at runtime (e.g., from Settings screen)

list.title: module:JRScene.registerOverhangData
list.description: Overhang controller. Drives the shared overhang from the router-active view's overhang fields, preserving the tabs-before-title ordering (prevents a title→tab render flash) and the bidirectional selectedTabId write-back (overhang tab tap → view.selectedTabId).

list.title: module:JRScene.reloadRoutedHome
list.description: Theme/locale change: force a fresh Home render through the router. Called from main.bs's reloadHomeRequested handler (replaces the old clearScenes + createAndShowHomeGroup). Navigating to "/" from Settings (the active routed view) is a component change, so clearStackOnResolve rebuilds Home from scratch — it picks up the new theme constants / reloaded translations.

list.title: module:JRScene.replayDeepLinkReplacingPlayer
list.description:
A deep link arrived while a media player is active. Two steps:

  1. tear the player down synchronously (stop + report to the server) so nothing keeps decoding;
  2. navigate Home, then to the new content, via the reliable navigateTo PROMISE chain (navigateChainStep). Navigating "/" tears the player host down (Home is clearStackOnResolve, so the stack — player host included — is cleared and Home re-mounts) and resolves at its NavigationEnd; the chain then mounts the target, which auto-launches. Back lands Player → Details → Home, the intended deep-link shape, with no stale prior item left behind.

We do NOT pop via goBack + a routerState-observer settle wait here (the old ADR-0020 primitive): goBack returns a bare Boolean (no promise to chain), and the routerState observer coalesces and reliably drops the terminal NavigationEnd, so the settle drain never fired and the cast stranded (proven on device). navigateChainStep rides navigateTo's promise — which resolves reliably via the router's internal chain, NOT the coalescing field observer — exactly as post-login deep-link replay already does.

list.title: module:JRScene.replayRoutedDeepLink
list.description: Replay a (deferred) deep link after login by navigating a SEQUENCE of routes, each step waiting for the previous to settle. Called from the main-thread replay helper (source/replayRoute.bs) via callFunc; routes is an ordered array of path strings. Used both for the no-deep-link case (["/"], a plain Home nav) and the deep-link case (["/", "/details/:type/:id", "/details/:type/:id/play"]) so back lands Player -> Details -> Home (decision #3). The queue for a /play step is populated by the stash producer (replayRoute / the deep-link handlers) BEFORE this runs; PlayerHostView reads it on mount.

list.title: module:JRScene.resetRouter
list.description: Sign-out / change-user / change-server: tear down the whole routed stack before main.bs re-enters the routed pre-login flow (loginRouter). Without this the routed views would linger and leak. initRouter() re-initializes a fresh router on the next successful login.

list.title: module:JRScene.resolveDeepLink
list.description: VALIDATE a deep-link id (a metadata fetch) BEFORE navigating, so an invalid id never disturbs the active session — it just toasts. args = { itemId, action, isPlayback, homeFirst, replacePlayer, detailsRoute } from source/replayRoute.bs. homeFirst (post-login/cold): land on Home first so an invalid id toasts on Home (good UX). On a valid id, onDeepLinkResolved navigates (replacing an active player for a playback cast).

list.title: module:JRScene.routerGoBack
list.description: Render-thread sgRouter.goBack() wrapper for main.bs, which runs on the main thread and can't call the sgrouter namespace directly (it resolves the router via m.top's scene). Used after a delete confirmation to leave the now-deleted routed detail.

list.title: module:JRScene.routerNavigate

list.title: module:LoadCaptionTask.fetchCaption
list.description:
Runs on the Task thread via functionName. HTTP requests require a Task thread.

Uses raw roUrlTransfer + WaitMessage instead of rr_Requests(). rr_Requests_run() is a standalone function whose m resolves to the component's shared m AA, and its busy-polling loop reads m.top thousands of times per second. WaitMessage() blocks at the OS level without touching m. See ADR 0014 — the layering reasons there still stand even though this component no longer shares m with a render thread.

list.title: module:LoadChannelsTask.loadChannels
list.description: Orchestrator Task: submits to ApiTask pool and waits off the render thread.

list.title: module:LoadExtrasRowsTask.buildRowRequest
list.description:
The request for one row. Mirrors what each LoadItemsTask branch sent, parameter for parameter.

apiPipeline yields such an entry as undelivered, which the row reports as failed.

list.title: module:LoadExtrasRowsTask.castItems
list.description:
Cards for the Cast & Crew row.

The merge and the labelling happen here, on this thread, before any node exists: merging a person's repeated credits makes the row FEWER nodes to carry across, and castCardSpecs() resolves each distinct label once for the whole array rather than once per person — which matters because every translate() from a Task thread reads m.global.translations at ~93 us against ~2 us from the render thread (docs/architecture/async.md). The specs are plain AAs; only the nodes below cross.

list.title: module:LoadExtrasRowsTask.emitResponse
list.description:
Transforms one pipeline response and emits its row.

res is invalid when the request never got an answer; an HTTP error (res.ok = false) and a 200 whose body holds no list are folded into the same "failed" status, because none says what the item HAS. Only an "ok" carries a list the UI may act on, including an empty one; the rule itself is extrasRows.itemsFromResponse.

list.title: module:LoadExtrasRowsTask.emitRow
list.description:
Finishes a row (ordering, filtering, playlist shape) and appends its carrier.

Everything before the append is thread-local — the item nodes and the carrier belong to this thread until then. The append and the rowReady write are the row's two crossings.

list.title: module:LoadExtrasRowsTask.loadExtrasRows
list.description:
One thread services every extras row an item shows. It replaced a serial chain of one persistent LoadItemsTask per row kind, where each row launched the next from its observer — so row k waited for the SUM of fetches 0..k, and every hop rewrote the RowList's layout after rows already existed, which redraws its row counter.

apiPipeline keeps one request per pool slot in flight on this one thread, so rows now arrive in completion order. Display order is restored by the consumer, which commits nothing until every row has resolved — see ExtrasRowList.commitRows.

Pool readiness: apiPipeline does not wait for the API pool to come up. That is safe here for the same reason it is for LoadLatestRowsTask — ExtrasRowList is only asked to load once ItemDetails holds the item, which arrived through a blocking fetch (loadDetailsTask, or the deep-link resolver), so the pool is provably up.

list.title: module:LoadItemsTask2.correctVersionDisplay
list.description:
Rewrite this page's items so each tile's progress bar shows the version that would actually play. The rules and the measurements are versionResume's DISPLAY section; the requests are versionDisplay.correctDisplayProgress().

The cache spans the whole run, so the genre pass below reuses whatever the main query already looked up rather than asking again. The resume list is scoped to this grid's container: a library, or — for a genre or studio view — the library the presenter set as itemId. That resolves through a collection too (verified 2026-09-20 against a 12.0 server: a resume query scoped to a BoxSet returns its members).

list.title: module:LoadItemsTask2.executeItemQuery
list.description: Routes an item query through Build*Request() + pool based on queryType. Used for both the main request and the optional 2nd lookup for the # filter. queryType values: "liveTV", "studios", "genres", "artists", "albumArtists", "usersItems"

list.title: module:LoadItemsTask2.populateGenreRow
list.description:
Fills one genre row with the sampled items its request returned.

res is the pool response AA, or invalid when the request never got an answer — the pool was down, or the whole-run budget expired. An HTTP error arrives as a valid res with ok = false. Both leave the row in place with its title and no children, which is exactly what the blocking fetchJson this replaced did when it returned invalid: a genre that can't be sampled still belongs in the list, and removing it would renumber the grid around a transient failure.

list.title: module:LoadLatestRowsTask.emitRow
list.description:
Transforms one response and emits its row.

res is invalid when the request never got an answer — the pool was down, or the run budget expired. An HTTP error (res.ok = false), and a 200 whose body holds no list, are deliberately folded into the same "failed" status: apiPipeline distinguishes the first two, but none is authoritative about what the library HOLDS, which is the only question this row's contents answer. Only an "ok" carries a list the UI may act on, including an empty one (which legitimately removes the row); the rule itself is latestRows.itemsFromResponse. HomeRows leaves any existing row alone on "failed" — a populated one keeps its content, an unpopulated one keeps its loading placeholder.

list.title: module:LoadLatestRowsTask.loadLatestRows
list.description:
One thread services every latest-media row, at any library count. apiPipeline keeps the API pool busy — several requests in flight, one per free slot — while this task stays a single thread; the per-library task fan-out it replaced was a &h29 "too many threads" source on large servers (epic #728). See source/api/apiPipeline.bs.

Results ride out as appended children rather than a shared field: rapid writes to one field can coalesce and silently drop a row.

list.title: module:LoadSheduleTask.loadSchedule
list.description:
Orchestrator Task: fetches the programs for one block of channels and hands them back grouped by channel, so the guide can give each channel row its programs in one write.

A fetch of a block's whole time window, or of the part before what it holds, sends minEndDate (programs still airing at its start or later); a fetch of the part after sends minStartDate (programs starting at or after what the block holds). The server compares both inclusively, so an extension repeats the programs the block holds at its edge — the guide drops them (Schedule.applyPrograms).

list.title: module:LoadVideoContentTask.addAudioStreamsToVideo
list.description:
addAudioStreamsToVideo: Populate video.fullAudioData with the item's audio tracks.

Sources from the original item metadata (meta.mediaSourcesData) — NOT from the PlaybackInfo response. The /PlaybackInfo response can return a transcode-shaped MediaSource carrying only the chosen audio stream, which would shrink the OSD picker to a single entry (issue #500). The OSD picker must always list every original track so the user can switch.

list.title: module:LoadVideoContentTask.addNextEpisodesToQueue
list.description: Add next episodes to the playback queue

list.title: module:LoadVideoContentTask.fetchMostRecentVersionId
list.description:
fetchMostRecentVersionId: Ask the server which of an item's versions it would resume.

The resume query returns the version that owns the resume point, which is the answer the source order gives only from a primary (see versionResume.chooseResumeSource). Scoped to the item's parent — its season, or the folder holding a movie — so the reply is that parent's in-progress items rather than the whole of Continue Watching, and lean, because only ids are read.

answer, so the caller falls back to the order instead of asking again

list.title: module:LoadVideoContentTask.fetchVersionPositions
list.description:
fetchVersionPositions: Read each named version's own position into positions.

A version that does not answer is recorded as POSITION_UNREADABLE rather than left absent, so the caller's next pass cannot ask for it again and loop — and so an unread position is never mistaken for "this version has no progress", which would silently restart the content.

list.title: module:LoadVideoContentTask.resolveResumeVersion
list.description:
resolveResumeVersion: Which of an item's versions resumes, and from where.

The imperative shell around versionResume.chooseResumeSource(): that function owns every rule and says what it still needs; this fetches it and asks again. Same division as ItemDetails, so both entry points reach an identical answer — the split between them is what made the app name one version on the details screen and play another.

Reads ride apiPipeline rather than a fetch loop: the pipeline keeps as many requests on the pool as it has slots, so N versions cost roughly one round trip instead of N. Each reply is ~150 bytes against the item's ~17 KB, and nothing is fetched at all unless something is already in progress — so an item nobody has started costs no requests on the playback path. When the source order cannot say which version was played last, one more request asks the server (fetchMostRecentVersionId).

list.title: module:LoadVideoContentTask.setupVideoContentWithAuth
list.description:
setupVideoContentWithAuth: Configures video content URL and applies authentication

Determines the appropriate URL based on protocol and stream location, then applies Jellyfin authentication headers for internal streams. External streams (non-localhost) receive the raw URL without authentication to prevent credential leakage.

Protocol handling:

  • "file": Direct stream from Jellyfin server (gets auth)
  • Non-file with localhost domain: Proxied through Jellyfin (gets auth)
  • Non-file with external domain: Direct external URL (NO auth)

list.title: module:LoadVideoContentTask.upstreamPlaylistAnswers
list.description:
upstreamPlaylistAnswers: Whether THIS device can load a live channel's upstream HLS playlist.

A preflight for playing a channel from its own URL (getUpstreamHlsBlocker). The server reaching a URL says nothing about the Roku reaching it, and a Roku handed one it cannot reach does not error: an unroutable host or an unresolvable name leaves it buffering indefinitely, so the direct-play fallback never runs. A GET within timeouts.LIVE_UPSTREAM_PREFLIGHT_MS that returns an HLS playlist is the answer (isHlsPlaylistResponse); anything else keeps the server's stream. Raw roUrlTransfer on this Task thread, no Jellyfin auth (the URL is not Jellyfin's) and the URL is never logged, because upstream URLs carry session tokens.

list.title: module:OSD.onItemDataChanged
list.description:
onItemDataChanged: Reads typed fields from JellyfinBaseItem node and populates OSD display.

Replaces the old JSON-parsing setFields(). The item node is immutable - all metadata is read directly from typed fields (item.type, item.name, item.communityRating, etc.)

Content Type Detection (isMovie/isSeries): These flags determine which user settings control ratings display:

  • isMovie=true: Uses uiMoviesShowRatings setting
  • isSeries=true: Uses uiTvShowsDisableCommunityRating setting

Detection Priority (applied in order):

  1. API flags: Uses isMovie/isSeries from JellyfinBaseItem if provided
  2. Flag validation: Ensures mutual exclusivity (both cannot be true)
  3. Type-based: Recording types always classified as series content
  4. Metadata heuristic: Presence of seriesName/parentIndexNumber indicates series
  5. Default fallback: Assumes movie content if no other indicators

translation is taken as a SCREEN coordinate: the OSD is mounted at the origin of a full-screen view, which is the same assumption the right group's own 1830 origin already encodes.

The time goes through formatDisambiguatedTime() — the same rule ItemDetails' "Ends at" chip uses — so it picks up an am/pm suffix exactly when the bare <Clock /> beside it can't disambiguate (across noon/midnight, or beyond a 12-hour horizon).
