list.title: module:ObserverProbeSubject.selfUnobserve
list.description: Remove observers on this node's own value field, from this component's scope.

list.title: module:ObserverProbeSubject.writeAndReadBack
list.description: Write this node's own field, then record how many handler runs happened BEFORE the next statement: 1 means dispatch is synchronous for a same-thread self-write, 0 means it was deferred.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.DEFAULT_BODY_SPACING
list.description: The itemSpacings the XML declares on #scrollContent, named here because clearReportNodes has to restore it after a structured body widened it.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.DIALOG_WIDTH
list.description:
This dialog's OWN geometry. The vertical flow (padding, title, accent rule, gaps) is shared — see source/utils/dialogLayout.bs.

WIDTH is this dialog's to choose; HEIGHT is not, and used to be. The panel was a fixed 1602x762 on the reasoning that a scrolling body cannot decide its own size. That is half true and it was the wrong half: the WIDTH is what decides where the text wraps, and the width is fixed, so the text's natural height is fully known before any height decision. So the panel is content-derived like every other dialog now, and the scroll viewport reads the body height the flow hands back — clamped at PANEL_MAX_HEIGHT, which is the point at which it scrolls. A short description gets a small panel instead of ~200px of dead space; a long one gets 924px, which is 162px MORE than the old fixed height.

1602 rather than 1600 because a width divisible by 6 puts the centred panelX on the 720p output grid ((1920 - w) / 2 = 960 - w/2); computeDialogLayout snaps panelY. 1600 put every edge off it — the most visible chrome in the app's largest panel.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.REPORT_LABEL_WIDTH
list.description:
Structured-body geometry. Both label columns are fixed rather than measured: measuring the widest label needs a rendered pass, and this dialog already learned the hard way that nothing may depend on which pass it is in. Both are multiples of 6 so the value column's left edge lands on the 720p output grid. Wide enough that no known label has to wrap, because wrapping is the expensive fix here: a wrapping label must be render-tracked (it could be the tallest thing in its row), and tracked nodes are quadratic — see trackReportNode.

MEASURED on a Stick 4K, not estimated from character counts, which got this wrong in both directions — the longest string is not the widest one:

Total Bitrate 179px the longest ENGLISH row label Taxa de bits total 250px pt_BR Formato dos pixeis 271px pt / gl / es_AR Format slikovnih pik 285px sl — the longest by CHARACTERS (20), fits Formatu-edukiontzia 302px eu — the only real translation over 300 Hardware Acceleration 329px not a value we ship, but the shape of one

300 clipped eu by two pixels. 360 clears every string above with room to spare, stays a multiple of 6 so the value column's left edge lands on the 720p output grid, and costs the value column 60px it does not need — the longest value is a file path, which wraps to maxLines = 6 either way.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.REPORT_WIDE_LABEL_WIDTH
list.description: Reason rows carry a Jellyfin reason code in the label column ("VideoRangeTypeNotSupported"), which needs roughly twice the room a "Codec" does. Measured on a Stick 4K, the widest code in Jellyfin's vocabulary renders at 449px ("VideoRangeTypeNotSupported"; "ContainerBitrateExceedsLimit" is longer in characters but narrower at 437px), so this carries ~100px of headroom for a code the server adds later. Reason codes are never translated, so unlike the column above that measurement holds in every locale.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.SCROLLBAR_MARGIN
list.description: 12, not 8: the text column's right edge is body.width - THUMB - MARGIN, so a margin off the 6px scale pushed that edge off the 720p grid.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.SCROLLBAR_TRACK_INSET
list.description: Centring offset for the 3px track inside the 12px thumb gutter. The true centre is 4.5, which is both fractional AND off the grid — for a 3px hard edge that is the worst case, so it sits one and a half pixels right of centre instead, which nothing can see and the output grid can.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.applyLayout
list.description: Measure, then flow. Every input to the panel's height has to have settled before the panel can be sized, so each one that has not returns early and comes back through its own observer — the same measure-or-return shape JRDialog uses.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.applyScrollBounds
list.description: Derive the scroll state from the two heights the layout just settled. The body is clamped at PANEL_MAX_HEIGHT by computeDialogLayout, so maxScroll > 0 is exactly "the content did not fit" — this dialog never re-derives that ceiling.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.bodyLabelsMeasured
list.description: True once EVERY label this dialog expects to show reports a rendered height. Each label carries its own renderTracking observer, so each brings us back at least once — this only decides whether the pass we are in may be trusted, not whether another one is coming.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.buildReportRow
list.description:
One label/value row.

The label column is LabelSecondary and the value LabelPrimary, so the eye lands on the data rather than on the field names — the same emphasis split the theme table describes for text. The value wraps (a file path needs two or three lines); the label never does, which is what keeps the columns aligned.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.cancelDialog
list.description: Cancel this dialog from OUTSIDE — see cancelOpenDialog() in source/utils/dialogs.bs. This dialog is read-only and has no result field, so there is nothing to deliver: cancelling it is exactly closing it — but WHO closed it is still worth recording, because an owner that acts on closed must not act on a close the user did not make. Set before closeDialog(), which writes closed last.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.closeDialog
list.description: Dismiss this overlay. It is appended directly to the scene by FocusableOverview, so closing is a removeChild from our parent + restoring focus to the element that opened us (returnFocusTo).

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.hasBodyText
list.description: True when this dialog has anything to show in its scrolling body. Used to tell "nothing to render" apart from "not rendered yet", which otherwise both read as a measured height of zero and would park applyLayout forever.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.okButtonHeight
list.description: Rendered height of the OK button, or the shared fallback before it sizes itself. The fallback and the reasoning for it live in dialogLayout.bs, where JRDialog's row and QuickConnectDialog's row read the same one.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.onOpeningAnnouncementDue
list.description: Announce the dialog once the platform's own focus announcement is out of the way. The overview text IS the announcement here: this dialog exists to be read, so a screen-reader user opening it wants its contents, not just its title.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.onSectionsChanged
list.description:
The structured body arrived, or was refreshed.

Two paths, and choosing between them is the whole reason this dialog can carry a LIVE report. When the row ids are unchanged — the ordinary case, because a refresh re-reads the same stream — only the text of the value labels is rewritten. No node is created or destroyed, the body's height does not move, and neither does the user's scroll position or focus. When the shape genuinely differs (a transcode started, a section appeared), everything is rebuilt and the panel re-flows.

The in-place path deliberately does NOT call applyLayout(). A refreshed figure occupies the same single line as the one it replaces, so re-flowing would be a no-op that risks yanking the panel out from under someone mid-read.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.onTaglineChanged
list.description: Dynamically creates or removes the tagline label based on tagline text

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.onTaglineRendered
list.description: Tagline has rendered — its height is part of the body, so the PANEL changes, not just the scroll bounds.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.onTextRendered
list.description: Once the text has rendered its height is known, which is the last input the panel height was waiting on.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.reportNarrationLines
list.description:
The structured body, spoken.

Without this a report dialog announces its title and then falls silent, because the opening announcement reads overview and a report sets sections instead. Each row is read as "label, value" so the pairing survives being spoken — the two-column alignment that carries it visually is worth nothing to a listener.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.reportShapeMatches
list.description: True when the incoming sections carry exactly the row ids already on screen, in the same order. Order is part of it: two reports with the same ids in a different order are a different document, and reusing nodes across that would silently reorder the labels.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.settleLayout
list.description:
Lay out NOW, called by presentOverlayDialog once this dialog is attached.

The dialog is hidden until this returns, so there is no renderTracking to wait on — and none is needed, because localBoundingRect() answers while hidden. See dialogReveal.bs.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.trackReportNode
list.description: Every label whose rendered height feeds the panel gets a renderTracking observer, for the same reason the overview label has one: the panel cannot be sized until they have all reported. Only WRAPPING labels are tracked — a single-line label column cannot change the row height, and each tracked node is expensive twice over: it adds a settle signal AND a member to the set every other settle signal re-measures. Measured on a Stick 4K, one localBoundingRect() read costs 23.05 µs, so that set is quadratic in real time — 26 tracked nodes is ~15.6 ms of render-thread work per open and 46 would be ~48.8 ms. Do not track a node whose height cannot vary.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.updateReportValues
list.description: Rewrite the values whose text actually changed. Skipping the unchanged ones is not just a saving: assigning to a Label's text re-renders it, and doing that to every row five seconds apart would repaint the whole report to update two numbers.

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.updateScrollThumb
list.description: Updates the scroll thumb position to reflect the current scroll position

list.title: module:OverviewDialog.updateScrollbarFocus
list.description: Updates scrollbar thumb color based on focus state

list.title: module:PhotoDetails.MAX_CONSECUTIVE_PHOTO_FAILURES
list.description: How many photos in a row may fail before we stop skipping and make the user acknowledge it. Bounds the wholesale-failure case (e.g. no server URL): random mode has no end-of-list stop, so an unbounded skip would cycle silently forever.

list.title: module:PhotoDetails.onDestroy
list.description: onDestroy: Full teardown releasing all resources before component removal Called automatically via JRScreen.beforeViewClose when sgRouter permanently closes this view.

list.title: module:PhotoDetails.onIsRandomChanged
list.description: isRandom component field has changed

list.title: module:PhotoDetails.onIsSlideshowChanged
list.description: isSlideshow component field has changed

list.title: module:PhotoDetails.onScreenHidden
list.description: JRScreen hook. Used to ensure tasks are stopped

list.title: module:PhotoDetails.onScreenShown
list.description: The router creates this view; its launch data arrives as route.context (set by JRScene.onPhotoLaunchRequested). Apply it on first mount, setting itemIndex LAST so onItemContentChanged fires with itemsNode/itemsArray + slideshow flags already in place. itemIndex defaults to -1, so this runs once (subsequent shows are no-ops).

list.title: module:PhotoDetails.showPhoto
list.description:
Render the resolved photo, or handle an unresolvable one. Nothing else draws on this screen — no title, no overhang (see PhotoDetails.xml) — so a failed photo shows the user nothing new; the previous frame stays up, or black on the first one. During a slideshow we therefore toast and advance rather than stalling on a frame they never chose, and after MAX_CONSECUTIVE_PHOTO_FAILURES we stop advancing so a wholesale failure can't cycle silently.

A toast rather than a blocking dialog, and not only for interruption reasons: a dialog needs text metrics, and roFontRegistry is a MAIN|TASK-only component Roku refuses to create on the render thread. Toast goes through the scene's showToast, which is just field writes.

list.title: module:PhotoPresenter.PhotoPresenter#getBackdropMode
list.description: Photos use fullscreen backdrop

list.title: module:PhotoPresenter.PhotoPresenter#getOptions
list.description: Photo view options control slideshow and random behavior These are unusual - 4 options that set 2 boolean flags

list.title: module:PhotoPresenter.PhotoPresenter#isRandom
list.description: Returns current random state based on view mode

list.title: module:PhotoPresenter.PhotoPresenter#isSlideshow
list.description: Returns current slideshow state based on view mode

list.title: module:PhotoPresenter.PhotoPresenter#onOptionsClosed
list.description: Called when options dialog is closed Persist slideshow/random settings based on view selection

list.title: module:PhotoPresenter.PhotoPresenter#shouldShowPresentationInfo
list.description: No presentation info for photos

list.title: module:PlaybackEndReport.PlaybackEndReport
list.description: What VideoPlayerView reports to the server when its stream ends (classifyPlaybackEnd in source/utils/playbackEnd.bs). Every value but NONE posts to /sessions/playing/stopped.

list.title: module:PlaybackEndReport.PlaybackEndReport.FAILED
list.description: A stream that never played, or failed: a stop marked Failed, so the server leaves the position alone.

list.title: module:PlaybackEndReport.PlaybackEndReport.FINISHED
list.description: A stream that played to its end.

list.title: module:PlaybackEndReport.PlaybackEndReport.NONE
list.description: Nothing: this stream's end has already been reported, or a later state will report it.

list.title: module:PlaybackEndReport.PlaybackEndReport.STOPPED
list.description: A stream that played: the server saves its position.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.PLAYBACK_INFO_REFRESH_SECONDS
list.description:
How often the playback report re-reads the session while it is open.

5s rather than the 10s Jellyfin's web client uses, because that client's panel is a cache TTL on an always-open overlay while this is a dialog someone opened deliberately, usually because something looked wrong. The figure that matters — transcode speed — is a level to be confirmed, and halving the wait for the first confirmation is the whole benefit.

TWO GATES keep that from becoming an open-ended poll, and neither invents a number:

  1. The timer only STARTS when the report has live rows — i.e. a transcode is running. On direct play nothing in the report can change, so it never polls at all, which is most sessions.
  2. A tick makes no request once the device has been idle longer than the screensaver timeout THE USER CONFIGURED. That is their own statement about how long counts as away; a device with the screensaver switched off has said the opposite, and is never suspended.

Gate 2 is an IDLE threshold, not a claim about what is on screen. Roku suppresses the screensaver during video playback, so it may never actually appear here — the reason to lean on that number anyway is that the user picked it, not that the screen is covered.

Being wrong is cheap in exactly one direction, which is why the threshold can be loose: TimeSinceLastKeypress resets itself, so the first tick after any keypress fetches again — at most 5s of staleness, no state, no resume path, no key handling. Polling forever has no such recovery.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.abandonPlaybackDialogs
list.description: Drop the report and any track picker this view opened, delivering nothing. Both observers this view owns for the report go too — the timer's fire and the dialog's closed. The dialogs outlive this view (they are appended to the SCENE), so an unreleased observer on one would keep calling into a dead scope.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.currentMountProgressMs
list.description: How much of the live stream the current player mount has played, for the Live TV restart rule (newLiveProgress in liveTv.bs). The player measures it, since only it sees every position.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.destroyPlayer
list.description: Tear down the current player child (stop -> report stop to Jellyfin -> onDestroy -> remove).

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.exitPlayback
list.description: Leave the play route: pops this host off the router history (beforeViewClose -> onScreenHidden + onDestroy tear the player down) and resumes the view beneath (the item's details, or Home). Called on queue-exhaustion, playback error, and voice "stop". Replaces ViewCreator/VideoPlayerView's SceneManager.popScene.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.handleFocus
list.description: Router: take remote focus. Hand it to the player child if mounted; the player also grabs focus itself once content loads (VideoPlayerView.onVideoContentLoaded).

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.handleTransport
list.description: handleTransport: voice transport delegate. main.bs forwards transport commands here (the router-active view is this host, not the inner player); forward to the child player's own handler.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.mountPlayer
list.description: Build + mount the VideoPlayerView as a child of this host. Ported from ViewCreator.CreateVideoPlayerView; the only behavioral change is appendChild to the host instead of SceneManager.pushScene.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onAudioTrackSelected
list.description: Audio track selection handler

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onDestroy
list.description: Router: this view is being destroyed (goBack / sign-out resetRouter). Tear down the player child. abandonApiPromises() is injected here by the auto-abandon-promises BSC plugin (JRScreen.onDestroy's floor doesn't chain to SG-component overrides).

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onLiveStreamStalled
list.description: VideoPlayerView.bufferCheck saw a Live TV channel's buffering stall. The same two exits as a channel that ended: restart it (liveRestartOnStall allows that only after healthy playing) or show the error. A guard that declines leaves the player's buffer check running, so it asks again. The restart destroys the calling player synchronously, which bufferCheck is written to survive.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onPlaybackInfoDialogClosed
list.description:
The dialog closed — stop polling into it and let it go.

It reports that on its own closed field. It USED to be observed through parentNode, on the reasoning that a dialog which dismisses itself by removing itself from the scene has a detached parent — but parentNode is not a field on Node (its observable fields are id, focusable, focusedChild and change), so that observer never fired even once. Nothing cleared m.reportDialog, so the NEXT press of the "i" button found a dialog it believed was still open and quietly refreshed a node that was no longer in the scene: the report opened the first time and never again.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onPlaybackInfoLoaded
list.description: The session arrived. Compose the report and either open it or refresh the one already open.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onPlayerStateChange
list.description: =========================================================================== End-of-playback / queue advancement state machine. Ported from ViewCreator.onStateChange; the pop/push has become host-internal destroy/remount, and the queue-exhausted pop has become exitPlayback (goBack).

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onScreenShown
list.description: Router lifecycle (via JRScreen's onViewOpen bridge): mount the player for the current queue item. The launching code (QueueManager.playQueue -> JRScene) has already built the queue, so the host just reads getCurrentItem. Guard against a redundant call (e.g. screensaver-exit re-fires onScreenShown).

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onSelectAudioPressed
list.description: onSelectAudioPressed: Display audio selection dialog

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onSelectPlaybackInfoPressed
list.description:
User requested playback info.

Always re-fetches. The report used to be built once by the task and cached for the life of the player, which meant a DoVi buffer-overflow fallback (transcode -> direct play) left the "i" button confidently describing a transcode that had already stopped. Composition is cheap now that it happens here rather than on the Task thread, so a fresh answer costs one request.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onSelectSubtitlePressed
list.description: User requested subtitle selection popup

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onSelectVideoSourcePressed
list.description: onSelectVideoSourcePressed: Display video source selection dialog

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onSubtitleTrackSelected
list.description: Subtitle selection handler. selected is { index, isEncoded, trackName } — the "None" row is the one whose index is SubtitleSelection.NONE, which is why this no longer compares the row's LABEL against the literal string "none" (that comparison is why the None row could never be translated).

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.onVideoSourceSelected
list.description: Video source selection handler. Writing mediaSourceId triggers a video reload, so only write it when the source actually changed.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.playCurrentQueueItem
list.description: Host-internal advancement: remount the player for the CURRENT queue position. Callers (onPlayerStateChange next-item; VideoPlayerView channel switch) set the position + backdrop first. Replaces ViewCreator's clearPreviousScene + playQueue (which created a new pushed scene).

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.playbackReportInputs
list.description: Everything the pure report builder needs, gathered on the RENDER thread where an m.global read costs ~2 µs rather than the ~93 µs it cost inside the task.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.prepareToLeaveMount
list.description: The checks and screen-clearing every exit from the current mount shares — a stream that finished (onPlayerStateChange) and a Live TV stream that stalled (onLiveStreamStalled). Returns false when a guard says to leave the mount alone, before anything is torn down.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.releasePlaybackInfoRefresh
list.description: Stop the timer AND let it go. Kept distinct from stopPlaybackInfoRefresh because closing the dialog only pauses polling — the same timer is reused the next time the report is opened — while onDestroy has to release the observer.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.reportHasLiveRows
list.description:
True when the report contains something that can change while it is open.

Only the transcode section is live (speed, progress, output bitrate); every other row is fixed for the session and would re-resolve to identical text. A direct-play report therefore has nothing to poll FOR, which is the honest reason not to poll rather than a budget someone picked.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.reportNeedsPolling
list.description:
True when the report still has an unanswered question — either something that changes while you watch it, or something we have not been told yet.

Two ways to qualify, and the second is what makes a failed first fetch recoverable. Live rows exist only during a transcode. A MISSING SESSION means the whole transcode half of the report is unknown rather than absent, so the dialog is showing a provisional answer and has to keep asking; the first tick that returns a session fills in the status line and the transcode section, and if that session turns out to be a direct play this same gate then stops the timer on the next pass.

A direct play with a session in hand qualifies as neither, which is the case that must never poll — and it is most sessions.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.resolvePickedValue
list.description: The option the user picked, or invalid if they backed out. Clears the dialog slot — every result handler starts here.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.restartLiveChannel
list.description: Restart the Live TV channel whose stream ended. Same remount as playCurrentQueueItem, except that it keeps the restart count: every other remount (channel switch, queue advance) resets it.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.showTrackPicker
list.description: Present a picker built by source/utils/trackPickerOptions.bs. Holding the option set is what makes the result usable: JRListDialog answers with an INDEX, and values is what that index means.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.startPlaybackInfoLoad
list.description: One fetch of the live session, on a NEW node per run (ADR 0037) — a node that is still running ignores a relaunch. Replaces any run in flight, which is what a press wants; the refresh tick lets one finish instead (onPlaybackInfoRefreshDue).

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.teardownForDeepLink
list.description: A deep link arrived while this player is active. Stop + report the player NOW (synchronously) WITHOUT navigating — the caller (JRScene.replayDeepLinkReplacingPlayer) then goBacks, whose beforeViewClose -> onDestroy does the full teardown. destroyPlayer is idempotent (guards m.view), so that second teardown is a safe no-op — NOT a full onDestroy here, which would run twice and double-tear-down.

list.title: module:PlayerHostView.userIsAdministrator
list.description:
True only when the signed-in user is a Jellyfin administrator.

Every hop is checked because this decides whether a filesystem path is shown: the failure mode of a wrong true is disclosing something, and the failure mode of a wrong false is one missing row.

list.title: module:QueueManager.advanceTo
list.description:
advanceTo: Move a VIDEO queue to another item because playback moved there — the next one when an item ends, or the player's next / previous. The queue ARRIVES at that item, so it starts from the beginning on the viewer's explicit version pick (nodeHelpers.startFresh): a position saved on it belongs to an earlier session, and the viewer is watching in order. Resume is the Resume button's job; jellyfin-web's nextTrack also plays with no start position. Without this only a multi-version item resumed (its version chooser reads positions) while every other item started at 0.

Not an arrival: the item behind a Cinema Mode intro (followsIntro), which is the one the viewer launched, and Live TV, which has no position to start from.

Audio moves with moveForward / moveBack / setPosition and is untouched.

list.title: module:QueueManager.cancelActiveQuickPlayTask
list.description: Stop, unobserve, and drop the in-flight QuickPlayTask if one exists. Safe to call when none is active. The single teardown path for m.activeQuickPlayTask (reused by onQuickPlayTaskOutput).

list.title: module:QueueManager.cancelActiveShuffleTask

list.title: module:QueueManager.insertAfterCurrent
list.description:
insertAfterCurrent: Put an item directly after the one playing, so the queue reaches it next.

The Cinema Mode intro queues the item it plays in front of. Appending that copy to the END plays the rest of the queue first: measured 2026-09-19 on 10.11, a Play All queue became [e1, e2, e3, e4, e1] and the intro was followed by e2, with e1 played last. With one item queued — every other intro path — the end IS the next slot, which is why it went unnoticed.

list.title: module:QueueManager.isPrerollActive
list.description: Return isPrerollActive status

list.title: module:QueueManager.launchItem
list.description: Single-tap playback launcher. Routed views (Home rows / library grids / search / details extras) call this directly. Synchronous types build the queue inline via the quickplay.* helpers + playQueue (which routes to PlayerHostView); async types (need an API call to expand into a queue) go through QuickPlayTask.

list.title: module:QueueManager.launchPhotoAlbum
list.description: Launch a PhotoAlbum slideshow. isRandom = true is the Shuffle button (random slideshow); false is the Slideshow button (sequential). Sets the shuffle mode the onQuickPlayTaskOutput photo branch reads, then runs the loadPhotoAlbum task.

list.title: module:QueueManager.launchQuickPlayAction
list.description: Run a QuickPlayTask for an async playback action and route its output to the queue. Used by launchItem's async branch (item taps that expand into a queue) and by the ItemDetails playAll / trailer / instant-mix / slideshow buttons. Owns the task on this node's render thread. Clears the queue up front so the QuickPlayTask output (which appends via pushToQueue / set) starts from empty.

list.title: module:QueueManager.launchShuffle
list.description: Shuffle-play a Series / Season / Person via GetShuffleItemsTask (the API resolves the randomized item set off the render thread). Owns the task on this node. PhotoAlbum shuffle does NOT come here — it launches a random slideshow through launchPhotoAlbum instead.

list.title: module:QueueManager.moveForward

list.title: module:QueueManager.onQuickPlayTaskOutput
list.description: QuickPlayTask finished — build the queue from its output and play (ported from main.bs's handleQuickPlayOutput). Photo output still pushes a PhotoDetails scene; that moves to the /photo route in a later step.

list.title: module:QuickConnectDialog.OPENING_ANNOUNCEMENT_DELAY
list.description: Mirrors JRDialog's OPENING_ANNOUNCEMENT_DELAY. Duplicated rather than shared because BrighterScript consts are file-scoped and JRDialog's is not visible here; the value is one number with one reason, documented in full at its original (the platform's own focus announcement FLUSHES ours, and SceneGraph exposes no event for "the platform has finished speaking").

list.title: module:QuickConnectDialog.PANEL_WIDTH
list.description:
Layout is DERIVED and computed exactly ONCE, from the two blocks this dialog owns: the instruction and the code below it. Both are laid out through the shared flow in source/utils/dialogLayout.bs — the instruction goes in the SUBHEADING slot, because that slot's whole definition is "a lead line that sits inside the body's space, so the pair reads as one block", which is precisely the relationship between "enter this code" and the code. Using it means this component does no layout arithmetic of its own.

Width matches JRDialog's 762 deliberately: this dialog carries about as much text as an alert and should be indistinguishable from one at a glance. That is asserted rather than trusted — see the panel-width spec, which compares this component's rendered panel against a rendered JRDialog rather than against the literal below, so the two cannot drift apart silently.

list.title: module:QuickConnectDialog.applyLayout
list.description: Position the chrome and the two body blocks. Safe to run repeatedly; it returns early until every block it needs has actually been measured.

list.title: module:QuickConnectDialog.buttonRowHeight
list.description: Rendered height of the button row, or a computed fallback before it lays out (localBoundingRect is 0 until the TextButton sizes itself).

list.title: module:QuickConnectDialog.cancelDialog
list.description: Cancel from OUTSIDE — cancelOpenDialog() and presentOverlayDialog's supersede. Routed through resolveDialog so the once-only guard and the standard cancelled result both apply. The result records that it came from code — see JRDialog.cancelDialog.

list.title: module:QuickConnectDialog.centerButtonRow
list.description: Centre the row on the PANEL, not the screen.

list.title: module:QuickConnectDialog.closeDialog
list.description: Dismiss this overlay: appended directly to the scene by dialogs.bs, so closing is a removeChild from our parent plus restoring focus to the opener.

list.title: module:QuickConnectDialog.onButtonFocusChanged
list.description:
Announce the whole dialog once the platform's own focus announcement is out of the way — the timing is JRDialog's, measured on device.

The code is spoken DIGIT BY DIGIT (see spokenQuickConnectCode): it is a string the listener has to transcribe onto another device, and a spaced digit string has exactly one pronunciation where a six-digit number has two.

list.title: module:QuickConnectDialog.onKeyEvent
list.description:
The decision is buttonDialogKeyAction in source/utils/dialogKeys.bs, the same model JRDialog uses. Everything here is the doing.

This dialog has ONE button, so the model collapses: "cancel" and "resolve" are the same outcome (resolveDialog takes no index — backing out is the only thing the user can do from here), and stepping a one-button row lands back on the button it started from, so the step actions are no-ops rather than a focus call. stacked is false because a single short label never stacks.

Sharing the model rather than hand-rolling two lines is the point: a horizontal row swallowing up/down under modal containment is a decision this dialog was making by accident, and it is now the same decision JRDialog makes on purpose.

list.title: module:QuickConnectDialog.onTitleChanged
list.description: SET THE TEXT FIELDS BEFORE PRESENTING, never after — see the field comments in the XML. Each change handler only writes the label; renderTracking brings us back to applyLayout() once the new text has actually laid out.

list.title: module:QuickConnectDialog.resolveDialog
list.description: Resolve exactly once, then close. This dialog has only one outcome of its own — the user backing out — so there is no index to pass: approval arrives at the OWNER from the server, which closes this dialog with abandonDialog() rather than through here.

list.title: module:QuickConnectDialog.settleLayout
list.description:
Lay out NOW, called by presentOverlayDialog once this dialog is attached.

The dialog is hidden until this returns, so there is no renderTracking to wait on — and none is needed, because localBoundingRect() answers while hidden. See dialogReveal.bs.

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.closeSocket
list.description: Best-effort teardown of the socket child + its observers.

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.connectAndPump
list.description: Open the socket and pump events until it closes or errors. Sends a KeepAlive whenever the wait times out at the interval Jellyfin's ForceKeepAlive requested (0 = block until an event, before any ForceKeepAlive arrives). Marshals each dispatchable command to the main thread. Returns on close. Returns TRUE when the connection was ESTABLISHED and STABLE — it opened AND stayed up at least STABLE_SESSION_MS — so runReceiver can reset its reconnect backoff. A never-opened socket, or one that opened but dropped sooner than that (a flap), returns FALSE so the backoff keeps climbing. Threshold = the backoff cap (30s): a session that outlived the max backoff interval was clearly real.

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.dispatchBatch
list.description: Parse a long-poll 200 body (a JSON array of { MessageType, Data, MessageId } envelopes) and marshal each dispatchable command to the main thread, in array order. Returns how many commands were actually dispatched (0 for an empty array, a garbled body, or an all-ignore batch) so the caller can floor a pointless fast 200 against a hot-loop.

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.dispatchEnvelope
list.description: Normalize one long-poll envelope and marshal it if dispatchable; returns true iff it was dispatched. The long-poll contract never carries KeepAlive/ForceKeepAlive (the poll request is the keepalive), so keepalive is treated like ignore here — there's no socket to answer on. Reuses the same pure parseMessage as the ws path.

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.handleFrame
list.description: Parse one inbound frame and either answer a keepalive or marshal a dispatchable command.

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.hasDispatched
list.description: Dedupe ring for at-least-once redelivery. Records ids we've actually dispatched and evicts the oldest past a bounded window — a duplicate only ever arrives back-to-back (a redelivery on the very next poll), so a small window is ample. An empty id (the ws path, or a malformed envelope) is never tracked, so it's never deduped — those transports/paths don't redeliver.

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.httpGet
list.description: Authenticated async GET on this Task thread. Blocks up to timeoutMs for the response. Returns { code, body }; code = 0 on a failed initiation or a timeout. A fresh roUrlTransfer + roMessagePort per call avoids cross-call event bleed. NEVER logs the url — the Authorization header carries the token. Mirrors the raw-transfer pattern in LoadCaptionTask.bs / ServerReachableTask.bs.

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.init
list.description: Remote-control receiver (#666) — the ws:// "Cast to JellyRock" listener. See RemoteControlTask.xml for the lifecycle/threading overview. This task owns the vendored WebSocketClient node and runs the Jellyfin session socket off the render thread: open -> parse frames -> answer keepalive -> marshal commands to the main thread -> reconnect with backoff. It NEVER dispatches (that's remoteDispatch on the main thread) and NEVER logs the socket url (it carries the auth token).

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.isTerminalSocketEvent
list.description:
True when this event means the connection is over, so the pump loop should tear down and let runWsReceiver reconnect. Two signals, because the receiver and the vendored socket loop key off DIFFERENT ones:

  • on_close / on_error — the fast path, and the only one that fires for an error raised while the socket is still OPEN or CLOSING (a failed read, a rejected handshake). That lands here at once, ~30s before _CLOSING_DELAY would force the client to CLOSED.
  • ready_state = CLOSED — the backstop. The vendored task loop releases its Task thread on that transition (#728), but the receiver would otherwise only ever wake on on_close/on_error. Those coincide in the client today — every _close() path in WebSocketClient.brs posts one of the two — yet nothing enforces it, and no lint can see it (it is a property of the vendored CLIENT, not of the files lint:socket-thread-release reads). Without this arm, an upstream re-sync that broke the coincidence would leave the pump blocked forever on a socket whose thread is already gone: no crash, no failing test, cast silently dead.

opened is load-bearing on the second arm. ready_state is CLOSED before open() is ever called AND the task seeds m.top.ready_state from it at startup, so an ungated test would race that seed and tear down every connection before it could open. Whichever signal arrives first wins; because _close() posts ready_state before on_close, the backstop usually wins the normal server-close path — the outcome is identical either way.

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.marshalCommand
list.description: Marshal a normalized command to the main thread. Drops the bulky original 'raw' Data first (a whole ItemIds list for a series/album can be large) — the normalized fields carry everything the main thread needs. Shared by both transports; callers gate out keepalive/ignore before calling.

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.runLongPollReceiver
list.description: HTTPS long-poll transport (#667). Roku can't ws:// a secure server, so on https we consume the companion plugin's authenticated long-poll command channel over TLS (roUrlTransfer). The poll request ITSELF is the keepalive (it refreshes server-side session activity), so — unlike the ws path — there's no client KeepAlive to send. See docs/architecture/remote-control-longpoll-contract.md.

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.runReceiver
list.description: Post-login entry point (control="RUN" from Home.isFirstRun, once the session token exists). Selects the transport by server scheme: an http:// server uses the ws:// session socket (#666); an https:// server can't ws:// (Roku has no socket TLS) so it probes for the companion plugin and, if present, runs the long-poll command channel (#667). SignOut sets control="STOP", terminating this thread.

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.runWsReceiver
list.description: ws:// transport (#666): build the session-socket url and run the connect/reconnect loop until the session ends (token rotated, or control="STOP" kills the thread).

list.title: module:RemoteControlTask.throttleEmptyPoll
list.description: Hot-loop floor for an abnormally fast EMPTY poll. A compliant plugin holds an empty poll for ~POLL_WAIT_MS, so this never fires against it; a misbehaving plugin that returns an empty 200/204 near-instantly would otherwise spin the poll loop with no backoff. Sleep out the remainder of a minimum interval. Only ever called on the empty path, so it never delays a real command.

list.title: module:SceneManager.isDialogOpen

It used to check only Roku's modal channel, so it began silently returning false for every dialog in the app when the JRDialog family moved to scene-appended overlays. The OSD read that false and hid itself out from under an open dialog, taking focus with it — the dialog stayed on screen but deaf, and Back fell through to the player.

list.title: module:SearchResults.applyRouteQuery
list.description:
If the route carries a voice query in its context, pre-populate the search box (which triggers the search via the searchAlpha alias) and focus the text entry. Returns true when a query was applied so onScreenShown can skip normal focus.

onScreenShown fires on first open AND on resume, and the router replays the ORIGINAL route (with its query context) on a back-resume (Router.brs reuses view.route) — so applying unconditionally would re-grab focus to the text box every time the user backs out of a result. Guard on the last-applied value: a back-resume carries the same query we already applied (skip), while a genuinely new voice search carries a different query (apply). The box already holds the prior term on a resume, so skipping a repeat is also the right UX.

list.title: module:SearchResults.init
list.description:
This screen has TWO loads, and they are measured as two ledger runs rather than one.

Opening search and running a search are separated by the user typing, which is an unbounded wait belonging to the person rather than to the app — measured on .177, the RTA harness alone sits 1.2 s in that gap. One run spanning both would publish a settled dominated by how fast something typed, which is not a property of this screen at all.

So init opens a run that ends when the keyboard is typable (variant open), and every query opens a fresh one that ends when its results are on screen (variant query) — begin's documented restart semantics, a re-load being a new run rather than a continuation. The variants are what let a reader select between them; npm run measure --nav search refuses a median until one is named, and names both.

list.title: module:SearchResults.onDestroy
list.description: onDestroy: Full teardown releasing all resources before component removal Called automatically via JRScreen.beforeViewClose when sgRouter permanently closes this view.

list.title: module:SearchResults.onKeyboardFocusChange
list.description: onKeyboardFocusChange: Fires when focus changes within the keyboard subtree (including entry/exit). Clears stale backdrop when keyboard gains focus, and adjusts alphabet layout when the voice button popup appears (textEditBox focused moves the textbox up to avoid overlap).

list.title: module:SearchResults.onQuickPlayLaunch
list.description: Forward a non-navigable result to the playback launcher.

list.title: module:SearchResults.onResultRowsReady
list.description:
The result rows are built and on screen — closes the rows fill.

Reads the VALUE rather than treating the notification as the signal: SearchRow clears the field at the start of every build, so half the callbacks here are the clear rather than the completion.

Deliberately UNGUARDED against arriving late. The mark is delivered by a CHILD, so a keystroke landing between the build and the mark would open the next run before it lands, and this would then resolve a fill that run never declared. resolve already handles that safely on its own — it warns and returns WITHOUT counting, and the next run still declares and closes its own rows — so the only thing a guard here would buy is silence, and the warning is the one signal that would ever tell anyone the race is real. Unobserved on .177 across two keystroke intervals; if screen-load unbalanced ever names rows, that is the race, and the tripwire is worth more than the suppressed edge case.

list.title: module:SearchResults.onSearchItemFocused
list.description: onSearchItemFocused: Update backdrop when search result is focused

list.title: module:SearchResults.onSearchItemSelected
list.description: A search result was selected — navigate to its route (rich node as context). Non-navigable results fall through to playback.

list.title: module:SearchRow.applyRowSizes
list.description: Applies per-row slot sizes, heights, and spacings to the RowList. Infers each row's slot size from its first item's type. Must be called after all rows are added to the content node.

list.title: module:SearchRow.getSlotSizeForType
list.description: Returns the appropriate slot size for a given Jellyfin item type. WIDE (16:9) — Episode, Video, MusicVideo, PhotoAlbum, Photo SQUARE (1:1) — Music types, Playlist, Program, TvChannel, Recording PORTRAIT (2:3) — all others (Movie, Series, Person, BoxSet, etc.)

list.title: module:SearchTask.searchMedia
list.description:
Searches multiple Jellyfin endpoints for media matching the query. Runs on SearchTask thread — fetchJson blocks waiting for ApiPool responses. Every result echoes the query it ANSWERS. The caller gives each keystroke a new node and drops a delivery from any node it has since replaced (SearchResults.loadResults); the echo is what that drop logs, so a superseded delivery names the query it answered. Taken from the local the search actually ran with, so the echo and the items cannot disagree.

⚠️ m.top.results is assigned ONCE, below, as this function's last act — and that is load-bearing, not incidental. It is what lets the caller's control = "stop" prevent a superseded query from delivering at all (measured: 12 keystrokes, 6 deliveries, every one current). Publishing partial results as each fetch lands would widen the window of superseded deliveries that SearchResults.loadResults has to drop.

list.title: module:ServerDiscoveryTask.FetchServerIds
list.description:
Fetch server IDs and names from /system/info/public for all discovered servers. All requests are fired in parallel on a shared port and collected within a 5s budget. Also strips the URL scheme to produce originalUrl (e.g. "192.168.1.100:8096") so:

  • users see clean URLs in the server picker (no "http://" prefix)
  • inferServerUrl() can re-probe the correct protocol on each connection, automatically picking up HTTPS if the server has been upgraded since last save

list.title: module:ServerDiscoveryTask.init
list.description: Task used to discover jellyfin servers on the local network

list.title: module:ServerReachableTask.init
list.description:
Off-thread reachability probe for a SAVED server we are about to switch to.

A deep-link server switch tears down the current session before re-authing against the target. If the target is offline, that would strand the user — so we pre-flight it with a non-destructive GET to its public system-info endpoint BEFORE any teardown. This runs on a Task thread (raw roUrlTransfer, no Jellyfin auth) rather than the API pool because the probe targets a DIFFERENT server than the active session: the pool would leak the current session's auth token cross-server and assumes m.global.server. See docs/architecture/api.md (Pattern 4) and docs/architecture/navigation.md ("Deep links").

list.title: module:ServerReachableTask.isServerReachable
list.description: Non-destructive: a raw GET to the saved canonical URL's public system-info endpoint. Does NOT touch m.global.server (unlike server.UpdateURL). Returns true only on HTTP 200 + a genuine Jellyfin server response, false on any error or an 8s timeout.

list.title: module:SideEffectTask.processNewChildren
list.description: Execute every unprocessed child's request AA in FIFO order, then prune processed children so the tree doesn't grow unbounded over a long session.

list.title: module:SideEffectTask.runSideEffectLoop
list.description:
Tier 2 fire-and-forget writer — FIFO children-as-vehicle queue (Architecture C, continuous-server). Mirrors ApiQueueTask, minus the slot pool and response routing: side effects have no response to deliver, so each request executes inline on this single thread in append order (serialised, must-complete: mark watched, playstate, favorite, …).

Why children instead of the old shared 'request' field: SceneGraph coalesces port events when a field is written rapidly from the render thread. Two back-to-back SubmitSideEffect() calls could merge into one event, and the second 'request' write clobbered the first before this thread read it — silently dropping a POST (issue #744: the capabilities POST lost behind the cold-launch /pair POST). Children are immune: even if wake-up events coalesce, we read ALL pending children from the node tree, so no request is ever lost regardless of timing.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.BADGE_ICON_NONE
list.description: Which icon a badge draws. A slot can show either, so both Posters exist in every slot with their uri assigned ONCE — see buildBadgePool.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.BADGE_ICON_SIZE
list.description: Badge icons render at the badge line's cap height so they optically match the label beside them rather than towering over it.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.BADGE_POOL_SIZE
list.description: Badge slots pre-allocated per row, sized to the most badges a single row of this type can carry so the pool never grows mid-scroll.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.badgesFor
list.description:
badgesFor: The flags that sit at the right of the meta line, most significant first.

Order is significance order, and that is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: when a row cannot fit every badge, the ones dropped are the last in this list (see placeBadges).

Only truths worth acting on get a badge. "Perfect match" leads because a hash-matched subtitle is the one signal that reliably predicts sync; the translation/impairment flags follow because they change whether the file is the right KIND of subtitle, not just whether it fits.

Each badge is an icon plus its label. The icons carry the meaning at a glance and the words disambiguate them, which matters because "perfect match" is not self-evident from a star alone. Colour does the ranking: the star takes colorPrimary because it is the signal worth acting on, everything else takes colorTextSecondary so it reads as a qualifier rather than a recommendation.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.buildBadgePool
list.description:
buildBadgePool: Create the badge nodes ONCE.

MarkupList recycles a small set of row components as the list scrolls, writing a new itemContent into each. The first draft tore down and rebuilt every badge child on each of those writes, so a single scroll step cost a burst of node create/destroy per visible row -- which is what made scrolling feel heavy. Nodes are now created once; only their text, colour and visibility change.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.fillBadgeSlot
list.description: fillBadgeSlot: Draw one badge in a slot. Chooses WHICH resident icon shows; never assigns a uri, which is what keeps a recycled row from rebinding a texture.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.groupThousands
list.description: groupThousands: 561277 -> "561,277". Download counts span four orders of magnitude in real result sets, and unpunctuated six-digit numbers are hard to size up at 10 feet.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.metaLineFor
list.description:
metaLineFor: "561,277 downloads . pirosasz . 2012", dropping any segment whose value is missing rather than rendering an empty gap.

Provider and format join the line only when the panel flagged them as varying across the result set.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.newBadge
list.description: newBadge: A wanted badge with its rendered width, measured once per content.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.newBadgeIcon
list.description:
newBadgeIcon: one resident, pre-bound badge Poster, collapsed until used.

Starts at zero SIZE, not merely hidden, and that distinction is load-bearing: measured on device, an invisible LayoutGroup child still occupies its slot in the layout — hiding a 22px icon left a 22px hole plus its spacing, which is how a badge with no icon ends up indented from one that has it. Width is therefore what this row toggles; visible just follows it.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.onFocusChanged
list.description:
onFocusChanged: the marquee, and nothing else.

The focus BORDER and surface are the list's now (see the XML), so all that is left here is the one thing a shared indicator cannot do: start and stop this row's own scrolling label. The colour used to be re-applied in both branches to the same value it is already given in init(), which is a write per focus change that could never change anything.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.placeBadges
list.description:
placeBadges: Show as many wanted badges as the row allows, right-aligned.

Filled into the LAST slots of the pool, in order, and the unused slots are hidden. badgeRow is right-aligned, so the last slot sits on the row's right edge; a hidden slot still takes its place in a LayoutGroup, so leaving the unused ones at the FRONT keeps them out of the way instead of pushing the visible badges in from the edge.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.titleFor
list.description: titleFor: The release name, which is what a user actually matches against their file. Falls back to the language when a provider returns no Name.

list.title: module:SubtitleResultRow.yearFrom
list.description: yearFrom: The year out of an ISO-8601 timestamp, or "" when absent/malformed. Upload year is a useful staleness cue (sampled results ranged 2012..2015) and is cheaper to read at a glance than a full date.

list.title: module:TaskLaunchQueue.enqueue
list.description: Queues node behind whatever waits. False only when TASK_QUEUE_CAP launches already wait — launchTask() then reports a refusal.

list.title: module:TaskLaunchQueue.publishDepth
list.description: launchTask() reads this to send new launches to the back of the queue instead of past it.

list.title: module:TaskLaunchQueue.recordQueuedLaunch
list.description:
The queue's counterpart to the refusal trace in tasks.bs: present in every dev sideload, absent from every store build, readable from the port-8085 console:

?m.global.taskLaunchQueuedTotal ?m.global.taskLaunchQueuePeak

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.benchAaAppend
list.description: CANDIDATE (b) — the ledger held in GetGlobalAA(), BrightScript thread-local memory. No node field is touched at all, so this pays neither a rendezvous nor the array-marshalling cost of writing an roSGNode array field. This is the per-launch cost of an APPEND-ONLY ledger; the walk moves to the audit.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.benchAaAppendVerified
list.description: The same append, but RETURNING THE RESULTING LENGTH so the caller can prove the pushes actually happened. The first run of this cell read -0.84 us — i.e. below the apparatus floor — and "too cheap to measure" and "optimised away entirely" are indistinguishable from a negative number alone. finalCount decides it: it must equal depth + iterations exactly.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.benchAaRecord
list.description:
THE COMBINED CANDIDATE — the ledger held in GetGlobalAA (free storage, no node field read or write) but still pruned on EVERY launch.

Pruning every launch is not gold-plating: pruneTaskLedger is what de-duplicates a relaunched node against the ledger, and a persistent Task node gets relaunched many times (when this was measured, ExtrasRowList alone relaunched its nodes 38 times). Skip it and the same live thread is counted 38 times, which would trip the watermark on an app running 11 threads. So this measures the honest floor for a CORRECT ledger that pays no node-field cost.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.benchCountNoLCase
list.description: CANDIDATE (c) — the liveness walk without LCase(), which allocates a string per entry per call. Roku documents the state values as lowercase; this measures what dropping the defensive fold would actually buy before anyone trades correctness for it.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.benchCounterOnly
list.description: CANDIDATE (a) — an O(1) monotonic counter on m.global. Needs no decrement because it counts LAUNCHES SINCE THE LAST AUDIT, not live threads, which is what killed the original counter design (it would have needed an observeField("state") per launch to decrement).

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.benchDrainBlocked
list.description: One launch-queue drain tick whose head the ledger refuses: the render-thread cost a saturated app pays per retry (ADR 0041). Only a depth of at least TASK_THREAD_WATERMARK refuses the head; stillQueued of 1 proves this measured a refused retry.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.benchFloor
list.description: The apparatus floor: the same loop doing the cheapest possible body. Whatever this reads is measurement overhead present in every cell above, and it is SUBTRACTED rather than argued to be negligible.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.benchNodeArrayPush
list.description:
CANDIDATE (e) — mutate the node's array field IN PLACE instead of rebuilding and writing it back. recordTaskLaunch today does read + rebuild + WRITE, and the write is what marshals. If reading an array field yields a reference rather than a copy, push alone is enough and the ledger can stay on m.global — which sidesteps GetGlobalAA's thread-scope question entirely.

verifiedGrowth is the whole point: if the field read returns a COPY, the pushes land on a throwaway and the field never grows. Cheap AND wrong would otherwise look exactly like cheap AND right.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.benchReads
list.description:
THE DISCRIMINATOR, and the single number this whole component exists to take.

Off the render thread the spec measures 1.56 us for a node the reading thread owns against 91-118 us for a render-owned Task node and 93 us for m.global (Stick 4K). If those three collapse onto each other HERE, every node the ledger touches is render-owned and the production hot path pays no rendezvous at all. If globalUs stays high, m.global is NOT render-owned and a production ledger pays a crossing per launch — which is the design fork this measurement decides.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.freshTask
list.description: ServerReachableTask's init() only sets functionName — no thread, no server. A never-launched Task node reports state = "init", which taskThreadIsLive counts as live, so depth is built without starting a single thread.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.gaaProbe
list.description: Writes this (render) thread's GetGlobalAA sentinel and starts the probe Task.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.gaaProbeResult
list.description: Reads BOTH directions once the probe Task has finished.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.ledgerCost
list.description: What the ceiling has cost so far, in real launches on real screens.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.liveCount
list.description:
The live Task-thread count right now, derived from the ledger launchTask() maintains in EVERY build — there is no conditional hook to be missing.

Returns tracked alongside live deliberately: a tracked of 0 means the ledger recorded nothing, while a live of 0 with a non-zero tracked means the app genuinely runs no Task threads right now. Those are opposite findings and a bare live conflates them — the peak gate asserts on tracked for exactly that reason.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.pruneLedgerNoLCase
list.description: pruneTaskLedger without the LCase() fold, to price that defence separately.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.runCell
list.description:
Runs one cell of the bench grid and returns its mean microseconds.

measured against so the caller never has to pair them up itself.

list.title: module:TaskLedgerBench.selfLaunchAndCount
list.description:
THE DISCRIMINATOR the earlier probe could not be.

gaa-thread-scope varied the THREAD and the COMPONENT at the same time, so an empty result was equally explained by "GetGlobalAA is per thread" and by "GetGlobalAA is per component" — and the ledger reading 0 across two render-thread components says the second is what is happening. This holds the thread fixed (render) and the component fixed (this one): launch through launchTask here, read the ledger here. A non-zero count means the ledger works WITHIN a component and the earlier conclusion was wrong.

list.title: module:TaskRelaunchProbeHost.configure
list.description: Configures the probe task before it is launched: how it blocks, for how long, and the input value its function reads.

list.title: module:TaskRelaunchProbeHost.dropHeld
list.description: Drops every held node. A thread still running keeps running; this only releases the references.

list.title: module:TaskRelaunchProbeHost.launchHeld
list.description: Creates, configures and launches one more held node. Returns { ok, node } on success, or { ok: false, code, message } when the launch threw (the cap's &h29 is documented as catchable).

list.title: module:TaskRelaunchProbeHost.release
list.description: Lets every invocation of the function return.

list.title: module:TaskRelaunchProbeHost.stopAndLaunchFresh
list.description: Stops the running task and launches a NEW node in its place, in one callback. m.top.task then holds the new node; the stopped one is returned so the spec can still read it.

list.title: module:TaskRelaunchProbeHost.stopAndRelaunch
list.description: The app's sequence: STOP, then launchTask, with nothing in between.

list.title: module:TaskRelaunchProbeHost.stopHeldLast
list.description: STOPs the most recently launched held node, from the render thread as the app does.

list.title: module:TaskRelaunchProbeHost.stopWriteRelaunch
list.description: The app's full sequence, which is not just STOP-then-launch: every site writes its INPUT field between the two (m.searchTask.query = query, m.loadDetailsTask.itemId = itemId). That write is why an ignored relaunch can still look right — the old run, if it survives, reads the new value.

list.title: module:TaskRelaunchProbeHost.writeAndLaunch
list.description: What a site with a persistent Task node does on every run after the first: write the input field and launch, with no STOP — whether or not the previous run has finished (MoviePresenter.loadLogo did this with itemId before it moved to replaceTask).

list.title: module:TaskRelaunchProbeTask.holdUntilReleased
list.description:
Counts the start, blocks the way blockMode says, counts the return.

beats advances every pass of the poll loop, so a spec can tell whether the function is still executing. The timeout only stops a failed spec from leaving a thread running for the rest of the suite.

blockMode exists because the app's Tasks do not all block alike, and the question a relaunch raises is what the OLD run does, not just whether a new one starts: pollLoop - wait() on a port in a loop, re-reading a field each pass (the original probe) waitOnce - ONE long wait() on a port, which is what fetchJson does inside the pool sleepOnce - sleep(), which parks the thread without a port at all waitForever - wait(0) on a port nothing ever writes to: blocks with NO timeout, so only a STOP can end it (TaskThreadSlots.spec.bs asks whether a STOP does)

seq is read TWICE: once at entry and once after the block. A caller that stops the task, writes a new seq and relaunches is doing what every app site does with its input field (m.searchTask.query = query then launch). If the relaunch is ignored but the old run survives its block, endSeq shows the run finishing against the NEW input — which looks correct on screen and hides the ignored launch.

list.title: module:TextButton.TEXT_BUTTON_ICON_GUTTER
list.description: Gap between the label's right edge and the icon.

list.title: module:TextButton.TEXT_BUTTON_ICON_SIZE
list.description: Affordance icon, sized 1:1 with the source bitmaps exactly as TrackDropdown does with the same 24x24 chevron, so the two dropdown affordances match.

list.title: module:TextButton.TEXT_BUTTON_INDICATOR_HEIGHT
list.description:
Selected-state underline. 6px is the same weight the overhang has always used for the selected tab, so the signal reads the same wherever it appears.

The bar is CENTERED in the gap between the label's bottom edge and the button's bottom edge rather than sitting at a fixed offset, and that is the whole reason this lives in one place now. JRTab's original version hard-coded +12 below a padding-derived text bottom — correct only at JRTab's padding of 30 and only while no minHeight is in play. Hand-copied into the subtitle panel at padding 24 it drew the bar 6px from the button's bottom edge and read as colliding with it. Centering makes the geometry correct at any padding and any minHeight, and reproduces JRTab's existing pixels exactly at padding 30.

list.title: module:TextButton.applyIconState
list.description: applyIconState: URI, size and visibility only — placement needs the button's measured size and therefore belongs to setSizeAndCenterText.

list.title: module:TextButton.applyLoadingState
list.description:
applyLoadingState: Swap the label for a spinner, or back.

DELIBERATELY CHANGES NO GEOMETRY. It reads the background's already-measured rect and never calls setSizeAndCenterText(), so a button cannot resize on its way into or out of a loading state — which matters more here than it does on IconButton, because TextButton now sizes the whole dialog family: JRDialog and QuickConnectDialog derive their panel width, height and row position from a button's isReady size, and dialogLayout.bs / dialogs.bs each hold a hand-copy of its padding arithmetic. A spinner that resized its button would move every dialog in the app.

Hiding the label rather than clearing its text is the same care: setSizeAndCenterText early-returns on empty text, so a cleared label would strand the button at whatever size it last had and never recover it when the text came back.

The selected-state underline is left alone. It only draws while both showSelectedIndicator and isButtonSelected hold, and no button in the app is both a toggle and an action that can be in flight; threading isLoading through layoutSelectedIndicator and onSelectedIndicatorChanged would add two guards for a combination that does not occur.

list.title: module:TextButton.hasIconSlot
list.description:
hasIconSlot: Whether this button reserves the leading/trailing affordance slot.

An icon and the in-flight spinner share it, so the question sizing asks is "is anything in the slot", not "is there an icon". Keeping it one predicate is what guarantees the width the label is measured against and the width the spinner is placed in can never disagree.

list.title: module:TextButton.labelLeft
list.description:
labelLeft: Where the label's BOX starts, given the slot the icon reserves.

The counterpart to textCenterOffset: that one says where the text's centre goes, this one says where to put a box of width buttonWidth - iconSpace so the centre lands there. A leading icon takes the left of the button, so the box starts after it; a trailing icon takes the right, so the box starts at 0.

Always >= 0, and that is the point — see setSizeAndCenterText. Offsetting the label node negatively puts a child outside its own component's background, and any LayoutGroup ancestor then silently repositions the whole button.

list.title: module:TextButton.layoutIcon
list.description:
layoutIcon: Place the icon for whichever role its side implies.

The two roles genuinely differ once minWidth binds the button wider than its content — which is the common case here, not the exception. A leading icon stays glued to the text as it centres; a trailing chevron stays glued to the button's right edge, matching TrackDropdown's trigger.

list.title: module:TextButton.layoutSelectedIndicator
list.description:
layoutSelectedIndicator: Place the underline under the label's visible box.

The label is vertically centered across the FULL button height, so its bottom edge follows from that centering — deriving it from the padding instead is what broke once a minHeight (or a smaller padding) was in play.

list.title: module:TextButton.onRenderComplete
list.description: Called when the component has rendered and we can measure the label accurately

list.title: module:TextButton.textCenterOffset
list.description:
textCenterOffset: How far the label's centre shifts from the button's centre.

A LEADING icon is part of the label — "▶ Play" is one phrase — so the pair is centred as a unit and the text gives up half the icon's space to its left. A TRAILING icon is a disclosure affordance belonging to the button rather than the phrase, so it is pinned to the right edge and the text centres in what's left, shifting the same distance the other way.
