list.description: A block there failed to load and is waiting to retry

list.title: module:guidePrograms.GuideSpanState.LOADED
list.description: Every block there covers the time around the left edge: a row without programs has none

list.title: module:guidePrograms.GuideSpanState.LOADING
list.description: A block there is still to be fetched, or its fetch is in flight

list.title: module:image.ImageURL
list.description: Returns an image URL for the specified item, or empty string if tag validation fails invalid/empty value, function returns empty string to prevent 404 requests

list.title: module:imageHelpers.GetBackdropURLFromItem
list.description: Generate backdrop URL from JellyfinBaseItem node

list.title: module:imageHelpers.GetLogoURLFromItem
list.description: Generate logo URL from JellyfinBaseItem node

list.title: module:imageHelpers.GetPosterURLFromItem
list.description: Generate poster URL from JellyfinBaseItem node Uses existing ImageURL() function with appropriate fallbacks

list.title: module:imageHelpers.GetUserAvatarURL
list.description: Generate user avatar URL from JellyfinUser node

list.title: module:infoRowFit.fitTextRow
list.description:
How much of a row of text items fits a width budget, and where to cut the rest.

ItemDetails' info rows are horizontal LayoutGroups of labels with a bullet divider between items, and a LayoutGroup never clips: whatever does not fit simply runs on past the budget. On the details screen that means into the logo, which sits at the right edge. This answers the fitting question ONCE, from widths, so the screen only has to apply the answer.

Pure on purpose: no node access, no m, no globals. The caller measures (a Label's boundingRect() is correct the instant its text is set, so this runs before the first paint) and the spec can drive every overflow shape without a device.

The cut keeps whole items in order and ends the row on the item that crosses the budget, narrowed to the space left so the Label can ellipsize it. Items after that one are dropped. If the space left is too small to read, that item is dropped too rather than rendered as a stub, EXCEPT the first item: a row is never emptied, so the first item always gets the whole budget.

ItemDetails: spacing + divider + spacing) or 0 when every kept item renders at its natural width }

list.title: module:infoRowFit.textLineWidth
list.description:
The width a line of text starting at textLeftX may use, given where the logo is.

A line that ends above the logo (with clearance to spare) runs to rightEdgeX; one beside the logo stops clearance short of the logo's left edge. With no logo on screen every line runs to rightEdgeX.

list.title: module:itemImageUrl.getItemBackdropUrl
list.description: Generate a full backdrop URL with fallback chain. Fallback order: item backdrop → parent backdrop

list.title: module:itemImageUrl.getItemImageUrl
list.description: Generate an image URL from a JellyfinBaseItem for a specific image type. This is the base function used by the typed convenience functions below.

list.title: module:itemImageUrl.getItemParentBackdropUrl
list.description: Generate a backdrop URL that prefers the parent (series/show) backdrop over the item's own. Use this for sub-item views (season episode lists, etc.) to maintain visual continuity with the parent detail screen. Both screens will resolve to the same series backdrop URL, which lets BackdropFader deduplicate the transition and avoid flickering. Fallback order: parent backdrop → item's own backdrop

list.title: module:itemImageUrl.getItemParentWidePosterUrl
list.description: Generate a wide art URL preferring the parent (series/show) wide images over the item's own. Skips item-level Thumb and Backdrop entirely; resolves directly from parent fields. Use this for episodes when the user prefers show art over episode screenshots. Fallback order: parent thumb → parent backdrop

list.title: module:itemImageUrl.getItemPosterUrl
list.description: Generate a poster (portrait) URL with fallback chain. Fallback order: item primary → parent primary → series primary

list.title: module:itemImageUrl.getItemThumbnailUrl
list.description: Generate a thumbnail URL (wide, smaller size). Delegates to getItemWidePosterUrl with a smaller default size.

list.title: module:itemImageUrl.getItemWidePosterUrl
list.description: Generate a wide/landscape URL with fallback chain. Fallback order: item thumb → item backdrop → parent thumb → parent backdrop

list.title: module:itemImageUrl.getProgramImageUrl
list.description: Generate an image URL for a Live TV program, falling back to the channel image. Accommodates the two-phase load constraint: program and channel are separate API calls.

list.title: module:items.ArtistOverview
list.description: Music Artist Data

list.title: module:items.AudioItem
list.description: Get audio item metadata (raw, no transform)

list.title: module:items.BuildAlbumSongsRequest
list.description: The Audio tracks on an album.

list.title: module:items.BuildArtistAlbumsRequest
list.description: Albums where this artist is the album artist (strict: AlbumArtistIds only), newest first. Does NOT include albums the artist merely contributes to — see BuildArtistAppearsOnRequest.

list.title: module:items.BuildArtistAppearsOnRequest
list.description: Albums an artist appears on as a contributing artist but is NOT the album artist of — Jellyfin's ContributingArtistIds, so mutually exclusive with BuildArtistAlbumsRequest. Newest first.

list.title: module:items.BuildArtistSongsRequest
list.description: All Audio tracks by an artist in any capacity (album artist OR contributing), so songs on compilations or with mismatched album-level tags still surface. Grouped by album then track; capped at 100 for prolific artists.

list.title: module:items.GetIntroVideos
list.description: Get Intro Videos for an item

list.title: module:items.GetItemLyrics
list.description: Get lyrics for an Audio item.

list.title: module:items.GetMediaSegments
list.description:
GetMediaSegments: Fetches media segments for an item (Intro, Outro, Recap, etc.).

Only available on Jellyfin 10.10.0+ servers. Returns invalid for older servers.

list.title: module:items.GetSongsByArtist
list.description: Get list of songs belonging to an artist

list.title: module:items.ItemDetailsMetaData
list.description: MetaData for an item detail screen — includes People, Genres, and Studios in addition to Chapters and Trickplay. Use this instead of ItemMetaData() when populating a detail view.

list.title: module:items.ItemMetaData
list.description: MetaData about an item — returns a JellyfinBaseItem node.

list.title: module:items.TVSeasons
list.description: Seasons for a TV Show

list.title: module:items.applyLiveTvMinSegments
list.description: applyLiveTvMinSegments: For HLS transcodes that report no source duration (live channels), request ≥8 segments per Roku's recommendation. Gives ~48 s seekable DVR window.

list.title: module:items.applyMediaSourceToPostData
list.description: applyMediaSourceToPostData: Applies the media source ID or live TV retry flags to a postData object. Live TV is detected by an empty mediaSourceId. On the first attempt, direct play is not disabled so the server can evaluate compatibility (matching web client behaviour). On retry, forceTranscoding=true sets EnableDirectPlay=false so the server provides a transcode URL instead.

list.title: module:items.buildHomeNextUpParams
list.description:
buildHomeNextUpParams: Query parameters for the Home Next Up row.

On 10.7–10.10, a user with no watch history inside the cutoff gets the first episode of EVERY series (one per series, not a short list). DisableFirstEpisode=true drops those, but on 10.8–10.10 it also makes the server ignore NextUpDateCutoff. So it is sent only where it costs nothing: always on 10.7 (which has no cutoff), and on 10.8–10.10 only when Max Days is off. With Max Days on, those servers keep the cutoff and still add first episodes. From 10.11 the server returns watch history only, so the parameter is not sent. So a user with no history gets no Next Up row, except on 10.8–10.10 with Max Days on. That is intended, and differs from jellyfin-web 10.10, which asks for the first episodes.

list.title: module:items.buildPlaybackInfoPostData
list.description:
buildPlaybackInfoPostData: The PlaybackInfo request body, tuned to the version being played.

Split from ItemPostPlaybackInfo so the body can be tested without a server.

list.title: module:items.hasWatchedRegularEpisode
list.description:
hasWatchedRegularEpisode: Checks whether a series has a watched episode that is not a special.

Mirrors Jellyfin's own "last watched" rule for Next Up (played, ParentIndexNumber <> 0 or null), which is what decides whether a series counts as started. The client needs its own copy because Next Up's disableFirstEpisode param, which used to apply that rule for us, is ignored from Jellyfin 10.11 and removed in 12.0 (#925).

The REST API has no "not equals" filter, so the caller fetches played episodes sorted ParentIndexNumber,IndexNumber descending with Limit 1: specials (season 0) sort below every regular season, so a special on top means no regular episode was watched.

list.title: module:items.honorsDisableFirstEpisode
list.description:
honorsDisableFirstEpisode: Whether a server acts on Next Up's DisableFirstEpisode parameter.

Honored on 10.7–10.10. From 10.11 the server ignores it (#925), and 12.0 removes it. Send the parameter only where this returns true: it is registered as a version-gated parameter in docs/dev/jellyfin-endpoint-availability.yml, and lint:endpoint-availability fails a file that sends it without calling this.

list.title: module:items.inheritSeriesOriginalLanguage
list.description: inheritSeriesOriginalLanguage: Give an episode its series' OriginalLanguage when track selection needs it (needsSeriesOriginalLanguage()) — as the server does for its own pick. One extra request, made only for a viewer whose audio preference is "Original language".

list.title: module:items.optimizeAudioCodecListForSource
list.description:
Tailors a video transcoding profile's AudioCodec list to the current source's channel count so the server (and downstream HLS variant selection) can't fall back to a less-desirable codec.

Multichannel source (>2ch): Strips ALL stereo-output codecs (aac, mp3, flac, alac, pcm, lpcm, wav, vorbis). Without this, Jellyfin's HLS muxer offers BOTH the surround codec AND a stereo fallback as separate variants in the master playlist, and Roku's HLS player has been observed (via in-house testing on physical hardware; no upstream tracking issue at time of writing) to pick the stereo variant — defeating the entire point of having surround passthrough hardware. Caller must already have verified the device has surround passthrough before invoking with channelCount > 2.

Stereo source (≤2ch): Strips surround passthrough codecs (eac3, ac3, dts) plus aac so transcoding falls through to mp3. Avoids handing the server a surround target codec for content that's only 2ch anyway. If filtering empties a previously non-empty list, falls back to "mp3" (the intended target).

Multichannel surround target (issue #573): For a >2ch source, the stripped list MUST lead with a server-encodeable surround codec. Two failure modes this prevents, both observed on Jellyfin 10.11 via PlaybackInfo probes:

  • Empty list: Jellyfin's StreamBuilder omits the audioCodec query param, the server's InferAudioCodec falls through to the container name ("m3u8"), ffmpeg gets -codec:a:0 m3u8 and exits 8. Happens when passthrough is detected only via codecs not in surroundPriority (truehd/dtshd-only) so no surround codec is in the list.
  • On-device-decode leak: a list like "truehd,opus" (truehd un-encodeable for a non-truehd source; opus on-device-decode only) resolves server-side to opus, silently abandoning the user's surround/passthrough intent for a decoded stereo-ish path. Fix: prepend the user's preferred multichannel codec (playbackPreferredMultichannelCodec), clamped to a reliably-encodeable HLS surround target — eac3 or ac3 (dts is excluded: the server emits no audio stream for a dts transcode target). This is a no-op for healthy profiles (their stripped list already leads with eac3/ac3) and only rescues the degenerate truehd/dtshd-only shape.

list.title: module:items.resolveMultichannelSurroundTarget
list.description: Resolve the surround transcode target for a multichannel source from the user's preferred multichannel codec setting (playbackPreferredMultichannelCodec). Clamped to the reliably- encodeable HLS surround targets: eac3 (default) and ac3. dts is intentionally excluded — the Jellyfin server emits no audio stream for a dts transcode target (verified on 10.11), so a dts fallback would itself re-trigger the issue #573 failure. Both eac3 and ac3 are valid HLS audio targets in every video transcoding container (ts and mp4), so no per-container clamp is needed.

list.title: module:items.supportsLyrics
list.description:
supportsLyrics: Checks if the connected Jellyfin server supports the Lyrics API.

The /Audio/{itemId}/Lyrics endpoint was introduced in Jellyfin 10.9.0. Servers below 10.9.0 do not have this endpoint and will return 404. Guarding the request mirrors supportsMediaSegments() (source/utils/mediaSegments.bs) and lets the endpoint-availability ledger record this as a validated version-guard.

list.title: module:languages.languageBaseCode
list.description: languageBaseCode: One canonical form of a language code, for comparing codes written in different ISO 639 forms — "fra", "fre" and "fr" all give "fr", "sw" and "swa" give "sw". A region or script suffix is dropped first ("pt-BR" → "pt"), as resolveLanguageName() does. A code neither map knows is returned lowercased as-is.

list.title: module:languages.languageEnglishFallbacks
list.description:
Comprehensive English-name fallback for ISO 639-2 codes that the app does NOT have a UI translation for (e.g., "lat" Latin, "swa" Swahili). Used as tier 2 by resolveLanguageName() — translatable languages always go through translate() first; this only fires when no LanguageX key exists for the resolved base code, ensuring no recognized 3-letter code ever displays raw.

Names are the official ISO 639-2 forms. They are intentionally NOT routed through the i18n pipeline: these languages are unlikely to be a UI locale for our users, so the maintenance cost of translating "Akkadian" into Polish (etc.) outweighs the UX benefit. Users see the English name in any UI when an audio/subtitle track is in one of these less-common languages.

Cached on the caller's m scope after first build.

list.title: module:languages.languageTranslationKeys
list.description:
Maps a normalized 2-letter base code (or a 3-letter code for languages without a 639-1 equivalent) to the translation key used by translate() for the localized language name. Keys must exist in locale/custom/en_US.json.

Region/script suffixes (e.g., "_BR", "_Hant") are stripped before lookup by resolveLanguageName(), so en_GB and en_US both land at "en" → LanguageEn.

Cached on the caller's m scope after first build.

list.title: module:languages.languagesMatch
list.description: languagesMatch: True when two language codes name the same language, whatever ISO 639 form each is written in (see languageBaseCode()). Regional variants count as the same language.

list.title: module:languages.mediaLanguageAliases
list.description:
Maps 3-letter ISO 639-2 codes (T = terminological, B = bibliographic) and deprecated ISO 639-1 codes to the 2-letter base codes used by the app's translation system. Only languages the app supports as a UI locale are covered (see scripts/update-translations.cjs LANGUAGE_METADATA).

Why this exists: ffmpeg/Jellyfin pass through whatever the container metadata holds — most modern files use 639-2/T (e.g., "fra"), older or hand-tagged files use 639-2/B (e.g., "fre"), and some use 639-1 ("fr" already, no alias needed). MediaStream.Language is therefore not a single standardized format; this map normalizes to one canonical form.

3-letter codes that have no 2-letter ISO 639-1 equivalent (ckb, fil, gsw, jbo, kab) are not aliased here — they're looked up directly in languageTranslationKeys() under their 3-letter form.

Cached on the caller's m scope after first build to avoid reallocating on every audio/subtitle render.

list.title: module:languages.mediaLanguageMatchAliases
list.description:
ISO 639-2 codes for the languages mediaLanguageAliases() leaves out (it covers only UI locales), mapped to their ISO 639-1 code. For language MATCHING only — see languageBaseCode(). Kept apart from mediaLanguageAliases() because display depends on that map's gaps: languageEnglishFallbacks() is keyed by the 3-letter code, so aliasing "swa" to "sw" there would show Swahili as the raw "swa".

Source: the ISO 639-2 list (Library of Congress) as Jellyfin 12.0 ships it, Emby.Server.Implementations/Localization/iso6392.txt — every code with an ISO 639-1 equivalent that mediaLanguageAliases() does not already map. lint:language-coverage fails if the two maps overlap.

list.title: module:libraryViewFactory.CreateLibraryView
list.description: Creates a library view with the appropriate presenter for the given library item

list.title: module:libraryViewFactory.DeterminePresenterType
list.description: Determines the presenter type based on the library item's collection type

list.title: module:listTheme.applyListFocusChrome
list.description:
Apply the standard focus chrome to a list node (LabelList, MarkupList, or any other ArrayGrid subtype — they all share these four fields).

Deliberately does NOT touch fonts, colours, alignment or spacing: those belong to whatever renders the ROW, which is the list itself for a LabelList and the item component for a MarkupList.

list.title: module:liveTv.LIVE_EDGE_SEEK
list.description: Sentinel seek position used to jump to the live edge of an HLS stream. Roku clips this to the manifest's available range, landing at the live edge.

list.title: module:liveTv.LIVE_EDGE_THRESHOLD_SECONDS
list.description: Maximum behind-live offset (seconds) at which we still consider the user to be at the live edge. Absorbs 1-tick rounding flicker between the integer wall-clock (roDateTime.AsSeconds) and int(m.top.position) — both tick discretely but can be out of phase by up to 1 second depending on calibration alignment, which would otherwise flicker the UI between LIVE and -0:01 every second during normal play.

list.title: module:liveTv.LIVE_PROGRESS_MAX_STEP_MS
list.description: The largest forward step between two position notifications that still counts as playing (see liveProgressOnPosition). Notifications arrive every 0.5 s (the Video node's default notificationInterval); the headroom is for a busy render thread delivering them late. A larger step is a jump (the live-edge join, a seek) and counts nothing. VideoPlayerView logs every jump and a per-mount summary of the steps it saw, which is the evidence for tuning this.

list.title: module:liveTv.LIVE_RESTART_HEALTHY_MS
list.description: How much of the stream a mount must have played (see newLiveProgress) for its end or stall to count as a feed that dropped: the count resets, and a stall restarts the channel.

list.title: module:liveTv.LIVE_RESTART_MAX
list.description: How many times in a row a Live TV channel is restarted after its stream ends without having played healthily, before the player stops restarting it and shows the playback error.

list.title: module:liveTv.LIVE_STALL_REPROVE_MS
list.description: How much of the stream a mount restarted after a stall must play before its own stall restarts the channel again. A restart into a playlist that stopped growing plays what was left past the join before it stalls, and that counts as progress: measured 2026-09-23 on a Stick 4K against 12.1, 19.5 s with 4 s segments (32 s and 64 s windows alike) and 29.6 s with 10 s segments, so it grows with the segment length and soon passes LIVE_RESTART_HEALTHY_MS. Four times the 10 s case.

list.title: module:liveTv.UpstreamHlsRequest
list.description: What the playback request knows that the server's PlaybackInfo answer does not carry, for getUpstreamHlsBlocker.

list.title: module:liveTv.applyScrubToAccumulatedBehind
list.description: Apply a scrub-during-pause delta to the accumulated behind-live counter. Forward scrub (positive delta) reduces behind; backward scrub (negative) grows it. Clamped to >= 0 so a forward scrub past the live edge resolves to 0 (live edge).

list.title: module:liveTv.buildChannelQueueList
list.description: Build a queue array from a Jellyfin /livetv/channels response and locate the currently-playing channel within it.

list.title: module:liveTv.canRestartLiveChannel
list.description: Whether a Live TV channel whose stream ended should be restarted, given its count from nextLiveRestartCount.

list.title: module:liveTv.computeLiveTvBehindLive
list.description:
Compute seconds the user is behind the live edge using a hybrid play/pause model.

Roku's m.top.position for live HLS DVR streams keeps advancing during pause — it tracks the live edge, not the user's playhead. So position-vs-wallclock math cancels out to zero during pause and we have to switch strategies based on state:

During pause: behindLive = accumulated + (now - pausedAtEpoch) Wall-clock-only — independent of position so Roku's auto-advance during pause is invisible to us.

During play: behindLive = (now - epochAtPosition0) - position Position-math — self-correcting on scrubs while playing, where position genuinely tracks the user's playhead.

On the pause→play transition the caller re-anchors epochAtPosition0 so play-math continues from the same offset where wall-clock math left off.

scrub adjustments made during the current pause)

list.title: module:liveTv.getUpstreamHlsBlocker
list.description:
What keeps a Live TV channel off its own HLS URL when the server has declined to direct play it, or UpstreamHlsBlocker.NONE when nothing does and the channel should play from that URL.

Jellyfin 12.0 (jellyfin/jellyfin#17768) stopped offering direct play for M3U channels whose URL is an HLS manifest: it had been relaying the upstream master playlist through its own /Videos/{id}/ URL, where the playlist's relative variant URIs 404. JellyRock never used that relay. It plays the absolute upstream Path (setupVideoContentWithAuth), where relative URIs resolve against the origin, which is how these channels played before 12.0. The server's remux instead drops audio that arrives as a separate HLS rendition. If the device cannot play the upstream stream, the live direct-play fallback (applyLiveDirectPlayFallback) still retries through the server.

The server's "no" does not say whether 12.0 is its only reason, so this rebuilds the answer the server would have given before 12.0 from what the client can see. It overrides only an explicit "no" (SupportsDirectPlay = false) on an HTTP HLS source whose Path is an absolute http(s) URL that does not go through Jellyfin: not a loopback host, not the server's own host and port, not the LiveStreamFiles relay. And only when none of the server's older reasons applies: the tuner's "Auto-loop live streams", the user's remote-source transcoding policy, or the server's internet streaming bitrate limit. The tuner's "Simultaneous stream limit" is the one reason the client cannot see; the server still enforces it when the live stream opens. DASH is excluded.

list.title: module:liveTv.isHlsPlaylistResponse
list.description: Whether a response to the preflight GET of a live channel's upstream playlist shows the device can play it: HTTP 200 with an HLS playlist body. The body check turns away a captive portal or an HTML error page served with 200; RFC 8216 requires #EXTM3U as the first line, so only leading whitespace is tolerated before it.

list.title: module:liveTv.liveGiveUpCauseKey
list.description: The translation key for the error shown when the host gives up on a Live TV channel: a channel that never showed any video since the viewer chose it is not sending any, and one that did has stopped.

list.title: module:liveTv.liveProgressOnNewStream
list.description: A new stream loaded into the same mount (a retry, or an audio or subtitle change that reloads). Its positions are on a timeline of their own, joined at the live edge again, so they cannot be compared with the mark the previous stream left; keeping it would count nothing until the new stream passed the old stream's furthest position. The progress already made stays.

list.title: module:liveTv.liveProgressOnPosition
list.description:
One position notification. A forward step of at most LIVE_PROGRESS_MAX_STEP_MS past the furthest position so far is playing and adds to the progress; a larger one is a jump (the live-edge join, a seek) that moves the mark without counting; a step back (a seek back, a replayed window) counts nothing and leaves the mark where it was. The live-edge seek sentinel is not a position at all.

the caller's debug log

list.title: module:liveTv.liveRestartOnEnd
list.description: The channel's stream ended. Counts this end (nextLiveRestartCount) and returns whether the channel should be restarted; false means give up and show the error.

list.title: module:liveTv.liveRestartOnMount
list.description: A player mount. Only a Live TV restart keeps the budget, so a first mount, a channel switch and a queue advance all start a fresh one.

list.title: module:liveTv.liveRestartOnStall
list.description:
The channel's stream stalled (VideoPlayerView.bufferCheck saw no buffering progress). Restarts only a mount that had played healthily, the dropped-feed case the restart exists for; any other stall returns false (show the error). Unlike an end, a stall is only detected at least 30 s into the spinner, so the end budget's three restarts would keep a viewer waiting for minutes.

After a stall restart, "healthily" means LIVE_STALL_REPROVE_MS rather than LIVE_RESTART_HEALTHY_MS: a restart into a playlist that stopped growing plays its leftover and stalls again, and with long segments that leftover alone would pass the lower bar every time.

list.title: module:liveTv.newLiveProgress
list.description:
How much of a live stream one player mount has played, for the restart rule: the sum of the small forward steps between position notifications that took the player past the furthest position it had reached. Driven by liveProgressOnPosition from the player's position observer.

Why steps, and not the position at a state change: the first playing reports no real position (measured on a Stick 4K, 12.1: the live-edge seek sentinel in some runs, 0 in others), and a stream that plays until it stalls has no state change in between, so the position there cannot anchor anything. Why only NEW ground: at the end of a playlist that stops growing, the player replays its window before it buffers, so time spent playing called a stale upstream healthy and restarted it forever. Pausing and buffering take no steps, so they count nothing either.

The step fields are diagnostics for LIVE_PROGRESS_MAX_STEP_MS (see VideoPlayerView's log lines).

the furthest position reached (-1 before the first usable one); smallestJumpMs is 0 with no jumps

list.title: module:liveTv.newLiveRestartBudget
list.description:
The Live TV restart budget PlayerHostView carries across its player mounts, since how much a mount played is measured by that mount's player (newLiveProgress). liveRestartOnMount, liveRestartOnEnd and liveRestartOnStall hold the whole rule, including when each field resets, so it can be tested without a player.

isStallRestart: the last restart answered a stall and no mount since has played LIVE_STALL_REPROVE_MS; hasPlayed: some mount since the viewer chose the channel made progress, which decides the error's wording (liveGiveUpCauseKey)

list.title: module:liveTv.nextLiveRestartCount
list.description:
The count of consecutive restarts after a Live TV channel's stream ends.

A live feed that drops mid-stream surfaces as finished, and the player restarts the channel instead of dropping the viewer back to the guide. A stream that ends before it ever plays (an on-demand playlist listed as a channel, joined at its end) also surfaces as finished, and restarting it just loops. So an end after healthy playback resets the count, and any other end adds one; canRestartLiveChannel decides whether that count still allows a restart.

list.title: module:liveTv.noteLiveMountProgress
list.description: What liveRestartOnEnd and liveRestartOnStall both learn from a mount's progress.

list.title: module:liveTv.recordResultToast
list.description: The toast for a RecordProgramTask result: scheduled or cancelled, and whether it worked. A failed result that is not a record reads as a failed cancel, as the task reports it.

list.title: module:liveTv.repartitionPauseStateOnScrub
list.description:
Compute the new accumulated baseline after a scrub during pause. Folds the elapsed pause duration into accumulated first so the wall-clock pause counter can be reset from the scrub moment — otherwise a forward scrub to live edge would still leave the wall-clock counter adding to total behindLive.

Caller is expected to also reset pausedAtEpoch = now after this returns.

list.title: module:liveTv.shouldTreatAsEpisode
list.description:
Decide whether a video should be tagged as ContentNode contenttype="episode". Tagging "episode" enables the Next-Episode flow in VideoPlayerView.

Episodes and series items are always episodes. Recordings are episodes only when their metadata identifies them as part of a series (seriesId set) — a standalone recording of a movie or sports event should NOT trigger the Next-Episode prompt.

Recordings without a season/episode number but WITH a seriesId still count as series content (e.g. news bulletins or shows whose EPG omits S/E numbering).

list.title: module:loginRouter.beginLogin
list.description: Cold-start (and session-reset) fast path. Runs the saved-server resolution + saved- token validation WITHOUT showing any interactive UI, and returns a decision telling main.bs which route to bring the router up on (or that we are already logged in). Mirrors LoginFlow()'s startLogin: server block + the saved-active-user branch.

list.title: module:loginRouter.buildPublicUserList
list.description: Build the public + saved user list for the picker. Public users from the server, plus saved users for this server id not already in the public list. Mirrors LoginFlow 60-104. Returns an array of PublicUserData nodes.

list.title: module:loginRouter.enterDecision
list.description:
Bring the router up on (or navigate it to) the route the decision names. Shared by cold start, session reset, and the post-server-connect step. clearSpinner: pass true when navigating here with a blocking spinner up, so it stays up across the async nav and clears at NavigationEnd instead of being stopped early (which re-shows the outgoing view for a frame). The success branch defers to finishLogin, which carries the spinner to Home.

What paint means for preLogin, which is NOT a screen

Everywhere else in this app screenLoad.paint is a screen that rendered something the user can act on. Here it is the coordinator handing a route to the router: the user is on a spinner for the whole run and CANNOT act at this moment — the destination view has not mounted yet (sgRouter resolves at NavigationEnd, on the render thread, where this ledger's m does not reach). The destination's own paint is a SEPARATE run, the same shape search established for a screen whose two loads are separated by a user.

So this run's paint/settle split says nothing: every fill is a synchronous main-thread call that has already resolved by the time we get here, so settled lands on the same millisecond as paint — the query variant of search all over again. Read the fills. They are the actionable decomposition: which of the blocking round trips cost what.

variant names WHICH load, not which destination: start is a cold start or a session reset arriving through beginLogin, connect is a server submitted from SetServerScreen. The destination is already legible from the fills (a run carrying users built the picker), and one run per entry point is what keeps two loads that route to the same place from merging into one population.

list.title: module:loginRouter.finishLogin
list.description:
Login complete — run the post-login bootstrap (per-user font processing) and bring up Home. loadHomeScreen()/createAndShowHomeGroup() (main.bs) navigate the router to "/", deferring until font download completes when UI fallback fonts are enabled. The single transition into the app. EVERY login path converges here — password, no-password, saved-token and Quick Connect — either directly or through enterDecision's status = "success" branch, which is where the two bootstrap paths (validateSavedToken, the no-password retry in resolveUser) land.

That convergence is why the authentication check belongs HERE and nowhere else. user.Login() is a sub: it silently returns when the payload carries no usable id (session.bs hasValidId), and having no return value it cannot say so. Before this guard, all five call sites answered that by re-implementing a WEAKER check of their own — isValid(<node>) alone — and then booting the app regardless. A payload that satisfied the caller but not Login left m.global.user holding its setGlobals() defaults and put the user on Home with nobody signed in: no message, no recovery, and every request going out with an empty Token=.

One guard at the one choke point, rather than five copies of Login's own precondition — so a sixth login path inherits it instead of having to remember it. See user.IsAuthenticated() for why this reads isLoaded rather than the id/authToken rule JellyfinUser.xml states (those are written speculatively before auth, so they answer "yes" after a failed attempt).

list.title: module:loginRouter.handlePreLoginIntent
list.description: Intent dispatch — called from main.bs's event loop when a pre-login view sets m.scene.preLoginIntent. The payload is read off the active routed view.

list.title: module:loginRouter.onCredentialsSubmitted
list.description: Credentials submitted from LoginScene. Mirrors CreateSigninGroup's submit handler.

list.title: module:loginRouter.onLoginBack
list.description: Back from LoginScene. Mirrors CreateSigninGroup back (showScenes 170-178): return to the user picker if there were public users, otherwise drop back to server select.

list.title: module:loginRouter.onQuickConnectAuthenticated
list.description:
Quick Connect produced a session. UserSelect owns everything before this point — it initiates, polls for approval, exchanges the secret and asks whether to save credentials, all as render-thread promises — and hands over the finished AuthenticationResult. What is left is the one step that must NOT run on the render thread: user.Login() reads and writes the registry.

Deliberately the same two lines the password path ends on, because it IS the same thing: an AuthenticationResult carrying an AccessToken and a UserDto. The old Quick Connect ran its own login on a TASK thread, then re-fetched the user with AboutMe() and re-loaded preferences that user.Login() had already loaded — three round trips where the password path makes one.

list.title: module:loginRouter.onServerSubmitted
list.description: Server URL submitted from SetServerScreen. Mirrors CreateServerGroup's submit handler.

list.title: module:loginRouter.onUserBack
list.description: Back from UserSelect → change server. Mirrors LoginFlow 114-119.

list.title: module:loginRouter.onUserSelected
list.description: A public/saved user was picked in UserSelect. Mirrors LoginFlow 120-163.

list.title: module:loginRouter.reenterLogin
list.description: Enter (or re-enter) the login flow. Called at cold start AND on every session reset (Change Server / User / Sign Out). Re-resolves the pre-login locale first — without this, a changed global sign-in language would only apply after a full app restart, and the sign-in screens would render in the just-signed-out user's language rather than the device-wide default (isPostLogin defaults false → pre-login cascade).

list.title: module:loginRouter.resolveUser
list.description: Decide the user step given a valid server. Returns one of: { status: "success" } — already authenticated (fast path) { status: "users", users: [...] } — show the user picker { status: "login", username: "" } — go straight to manual sign-in enterDecision maps each status to its route; the decision carries only payload. Mirrors LoginFlow()'s user section (active-user branch + no-active-user branch).

list.title: module:loginRouter.routerNav
list.description: Thin main-thread → render-thread navigation bridge. clearSpinner (login paths only) keeps a blocking login spinner up across the async nav and clears it when the destination view mounts — see JRScene.navigateThenFocus.

list.title: module:loginRouter.validateSavedToken
list.description: Validate a saved auth token: set it on the local user and verify it with AboutMe(). On success, logs the user in (user.Login) and returns true. On failure returns false — the caller owns the cleanup/fallback, which diverges between the two call sites (cold start unsets active_user + recurses; the user picker falls through to a no-password login). Shared by resolveUser (cold start) and onUserSelected (user picker).

list.title: module:logoLayout.logoDisplaySize
list.description:
The size the logo is drawn at, from the size of the bitmap that loads.

A small logo is scaled up to limits.minHeight, keeping aspect, unless that would make it wider than limits.maxWidth: maxWidth is a hard layout bound, minHeight only a target. When capHeight is set, a tall image is then scaled down to limits.maxHeight so it stays clear of the text rows above it.

list.title: module:logoLayout.serverFitSize
list.description: The size the server sends for an image request bounded by maxWidth x maxHeight: scaled down to fit, aspect kept, never scaled up. Measured 2026-09-22 against Jellyfin 12.1: the served size is the scaled size ROUNDED to the nearest pixel (15 of 15 logos; truncating was a pixel short on 6 of them).

list.title: module:main.calculateFontScaleFactor
list.description: Calculate global font scale factor for fallback font

list.title: module:main.createAndShowHomeGroup
list.description: Create and show the home group

list.title: module:main.handleFontDownloadCompletion
list.description: Handle font download completion and optionally calculate scale factor

list.title: module:main.handleMenuAction
list.description: Shared handler for menu actions from both the OptionsSlider and the user dropdown. OPEN_SEARCH / OPEN_SETTINGS are not handled here — Home navigates to those routes directly (navigateTo runs on the render thread, which main.bs is not). Only the session-ending actions remain. Each tears down the routed Home (resetRouter) and re-enters the login flow IN PLACE (reenterLogin) — no goto appStart, since the pre-login flow is routed and driven by the same unified event loop.

list.title: module:main.initializeFallbackFont
list.description: Initialize fallback font download process

list.title: module:main.loadHomeScreen
list.description: Load the home screen - may wait for font processing if UI fallback fonts are enabled

list.title: module:mediaDisplayTitle.formatAudioChannels
list.description: formatAudioChannels: Convert channel count integer to display format Ignores ChannelLayout field since it can return inconsistent strings (e.g., "stereo")

list.title: module:mediaDisplayTitle.formatAudioDisplayTitle
list.description: formatAudioDisplayTitle: Build a display title for an audio stream Format: "Language CODEC CHANNELS" or "Language CODEC CHANNELS (Default)"

list.title: module:mediaDisplayTitle.formatSubtitleDisplayTitle
list.description: formatSubtitleDisplayTitle: Build a display title for a subtitle stream Format: "Language CODEC", optionally followed by a parenthesised flag list — "English SUBRIP (Hearing impaired)", "English SUBRIP (Hearing impaired, Forced)". Forced takes precedence over default if both are set.

list.title: module:mediaDisplayTitle.formatVideoDisplayTitle
list.description: formatVideoDisplayTitle: Build a display title for a video stream Format: "RESOLUTION CODEC" or "RESOLUTION CODEC RANGETYPE" (when HDR)

list.title: module:mediaDisplayTitle.formatVideoRangeLabel
list.description:
formatVideoRangeLabel: The dynamic-range label for a video stream.

Extracted from formatVideoDisplayTitle so the playback-info report can name the same range the track pickers do, rather than growing a second copy of the Dolby Vision profile/compatibility formatting.

Callers differ in one way, and it is deliberate that this function does NOT decide it: formatVideoDisplayTitle only asks for a label when VideoRange is "HDR", because "1080p H264 SDR" is noise in a picker row. The report asks unconditionally, because "SDR" is exactly what it needs to render on the target side of a tone-mapping transcode.

VideoRangeType is a 10.8+ field, so on the floor server this falls back to the coarse VideoRange ("SDR" / "HDR") that has existed throughout.

list.title: module:mediaDisplayTitle.getVideoResolutionLabel
list.description: getVideoResolutionLabel: Determine resolution label from video dimensions Resolution thresholds check width OR height (either can qualify) 4K never gets p/i suffix. All other resolutions get "p" or "i" based on interlacing.

list.title: module:mediaDisplayTitle.resolveLanguageName
list.description:
resolveLanguageName: Convert a media stream language code to a localized display name.

MediaStream.Language passes through whatever the container metadata holds — ffmpeg/Jellyfin do not normalize, so real-world inputs include ISO 639-2/T ("fra"), 639-2/B ("fre"), 639-1 ("fr"), and BCP-47 tags ("fr-FR", "pt_BR").

Three-tier resolution chain:

  1. Lowercase + strip after first "-" or "_" (drop region/script suffix)
  2. "und" / "zxx" → "" — caller omits the language label
  3. Alias map → normalize 3-letter / deprecated codes to a base form
  4. Tier 1: translationKey lookup → translate() — localized to user's UI
  5. Tier 2: English-name fallback → covers every other ISO 639-2 code
  6. Tier 3: raw code passthrough — last-resort, preserves info

"und" (Undefined) and "zxx" (No linguistic content — instrumental music, ambient sound, foley) are both omitted: rendering "No linguistic content EAC3 5.1" as a track label is noisier than just "EAC3 5.1". The other ISO 639-2 special codes ("mul" Multiple, "mis" Uncoded) ARE displayed because they convey real information when they appear.

list.title: module:mediaSegments.SEGMENT_SKIP_END_OF_MEDIA_SECONDS
list.description: How close to the end of the media a skip may land before it counts as reaching the end.

list.title: module:mediaSegments.findActiveSegment
list.description:
findActiveSegment: Finds the media segment containing the current playback position.

Linear scan over the segments array (typically 2-5 items). Returns the first segment where StartTicks <= position < EndTicks.

list.title: module:mediaSegments.findSegmentById
list.description:
findSegmentById: Finds a media segment by its Id.

Linear scan over the segments array (typically 2-5 items). Prefer this over caching segment objects, since the segments array can be replaced during content loading (audio/subtitle track changes).

list.title: module:mediaSegments.resolveEffectiveSegmentAction
list.description:
resolveEffectiveSegmentAction: Resolves the action for a segment, accounting for whether it has already been auto-skipped this playback session.

A Skip-configured segment auto-seeks only on its first pass. Once skipped, rewinding back into it must NOT re-skip (that would trap the user in a rewind loop) — but the user should still get the manual Skip button. So an already-skipped Skip segment degrades to AskToSkip; all other actions pass through unchanged.

list.title: module:mediaSegments.resolveSegmentAction
list.description:
resolveSegmentAction: Resolves the action to take for a given media segment type.

Checks JellyRock per-type override setting first, then falls back to web client DisplayPreferences CustomPrefs value, then falls back to built-in defaults.

Built-in defaults: All types = AskToSkip

list.title: module:mediaSegments.segmentTicksToSeconds
list.description: segmentTicksToSeconds: Converts Jellyfin ticks (100-nanosecond units) to seconds.

list.title: module:mediaSegments.skipEndsPlayback
list.description:
skipEndsPlayback: Whether skipping to a segment's end would leave nothing left to play.

A skip seeks to the segment's end. When that is at or near the end of the media, the stream has nothing left to buffer: the player sits in buffering until the stall check reports a playback error, instead of ever reaching finished and moving on. So the caller finishes playback rather than seeking.

Deliberately independent of the segment TYPE. Any segment can run to the end of the file — a Preview after the Outro, credits, a commercial — and what makes the seek unplayable is where it lands, not what the segment was called.

list.title: module:mediaSegments.supportsMediaSegments
list.description:
supportsMediaSegments: Checks if the connected Jellyfin server supports the MediaSegments API.

The /MediaSegments/{itemId} endpoint was introduced in Jellyfin 10.10.0. Servers below 10.10.0 do not have this endpoint and will return 404.
