list.title: module:streamSelection.JellyfinLanguage
list.description: JellyfinLanguage: ISO 639-2 three-letter language codes used by Jellyfin Only includes languages supported by Roku OS locales

list.title: module:streamSelection.ORIGINAL_LANGUAGE_PREFERENCE
list.description: The web client's "Original language" audio preference (Jellyfin 12.0+). The server stores it in AudioLanguagePreference in place of a language code; it means "the item's OriginalLanguage".

list.title: module:streamSelection.applyLiveDirectPlayFallback
list.description: applyLiveDirectPlayFallback: Flags that a transcode retry is available for live streams attempting direct play. Live direct play may fail on Roku if the server overestimates compatibility. VideoPlayerView observes isTranscodeAvailable to retry with transcoding on error.

list.title: module:streamSelection.findBestAudioStreamIndex
list.description:
findBestAudioStreamIndex: Primary function for selecting the best audio stream

Selection priority when playDefault = true (Jellyfin: "Play default audio track regardless of language"):

  1. Filter by IsDefault = true streams (ignore language preference)
  2. If multiple IsDefault streams, use language preference as tiebreaker
  3. If still multiple or no language match, apply hardware optimization
  4. If no IsDefault streams exist, fall back to language preference → hardware optimization

Selection priority when playDefault = false:

  1. Filter by language preference (completely ignore IsDefault flag)
  2. If multiple language matches, apply hardware optimization
  3. If no language matches, apply hardware optimization to all streams

"Original language" (preferOriginal, playDefault = false) — as the server does, a stream the file flags IsOriginal wins: among the language matches when the item's original language is known, among all streams when it is not. The server ignores IsOriginal when playDefault = true.

Language matching: exact codes first, then the same language in another ISO form (matchingLanguageCodes()).

Roku OS Language Fallback: When preferredLanguage is blank/empty, automatically uses the Roku device's OS language (from m.global.device.locale) as fallback for better out-of-box experience (see issue #179). Not with preferOriginal: the viewer asked for the original, and the locale is usually the dub, so no language rule applies instead.

Hardware optimization:

  • Prefer streams matching device's max channel capability
  • Among matches, prefer direct-playable codecs
  • Fall back intelligently based on channel counts

list.title: module:streamSelection.findBestVideoSource
list.description:
findBestVideoSource: Selects the optimal MediaSource for the device's capabilities

Scoring algorithm:

  1. Resolution fit (primary): Prefer highest resolution at or below device max. Sources exceeding device max receive a penalty (will likely transcode).
  2. HDR match (secondary): If device supports HDR, prefer HDR sources. If device does NOT support HDR, prefer SDR (avoids tone-mapping transcode).
  3. Direct play (tertiary): Prefer sources the server says can direct play.
  4. Bitrate (tiebreaker): Higher bitrate wins among otherwise-equal sources.

list.title: module:streamSelection.findBestVideoSourceAmongIds
list.description:
findBestVideoSourceAmongIds: Best source for this device among a NAMED SUBSET of an item's versions.

The tie-break half of versionResume.chooseResumeSource(): that module decides which versions are at the same place and so compete on quality, but it is pure by contract and has no device knowledge, so it hands the tie back as ids. Scoring runs over just those versions, because the best of a subset is not the best overall — a 4K version nobody has started must not win a tie between two the viewer is actually partway through.

list.title: module:streamSelection.findDefaultSubtitleStreamIndex
list.description:
findDefaultSubtitleStreamIndex: Determine which subtitle stream will be auto-selected during playback Mirrors the selection logic in defaultSubtitleTrackFromVid() and sortSubtitles() (Subtitles.bs) for use on the render thread without requiring playback-specific dependencies (buildURL, etc.)

Selection logic (by subtitleMode): "none" → No subtitles "default" → First forced or default subtitle matching preferred language "always" → First non-forced subtitle matching preferred language; fallback to forced/default "onlyforced"→ First forced subtitle matching preferred language "smart" → First non-forced subtitle when audio language differs from preference; fallback to forced/default

Priority ordering: forced > default > normal; preferred language first within each category Text subtitles are tried first; non-text only used when playbackSubsOnlyText is false

list.title: module:streamSelection.findDirectPlayableStreamByChannelCount
list.description: findDirectPlayableStreamByChannelCount: Finds a direct-playable stream with specific channel count

list.title: module:streamSelection.getDeviceAudioCapabilities
list.description:
getDeviceAudioCapabilities: Detects device audio codec and channel support

Strategy:

  • Use combined check (no PassThru) for 6-channel and below (safe, checks both)
  • ALWAYS verify 8-channel with PassThru: 1 (combined check can lie)
  • Roku max native decode is 6 channels (varies by model)
  • 8-channel requires HDMI passthrough to receiver/soundbar

maxChannels (integer: 2, 6, or 8) - Maximum supported audio channels supports8Channel (boolean) - True if HDMI passthrough supports 8-channel audio

list.title: module:streamSelection.getDeviceVideoCapabilities
list.description:
getDeviceVideoCapabilities: Detects device video resolution and HDR support

Strategy:

  • Use cached m.global.device values for resolution (render-thread safe, no object creation)
  • Use canPlay4k() for 4K eligibility (HDCP 2.2 + HEVC decode check)
  • Use roDeviceInfo.GetDisplayProperties() for HDR format detection

maxHeight (integer) - Maximum display height in pixels maxWidth (integer) - Maximum display width in pixels canDecode4k (boolean) - True if device can play 4K content supportsHdr10 (boolean) - True if display supports HDR10 supportsDolbyVision (boolean) - True if display supports Dolby Vision supportsHlg (boolean) - True if display supports HLG

list.title: module:streamSelection.getTranscodeReasons
list.description: getTranscodeReasons: Extracts the transcode reason codes from a Jellyfin transcoding URL. The server embeds reasons as a comma-separated TranscodeReasons query parameter. Used to detect VideoLevelNotSupported so a direct-play fallback can be attempted.

list.title: module:streamSelection.isCommentaryAudioStream
list.description:
isCommentaryAudioStream: Determine whether a stream is a commentary/secondary track.

Detection: case-insensitive substring match for "commentary" in the stream Title. Used by findBestAudioStreamIndex() to deprioritize commentary tracks during auto-selection so a director's-commentary stereo track doesn't outrank the main multichannel track on a stereo device (issue #500).

list.title: module:streamSelection.isLanguageMatch
list.description: isLanguageMatch: Whether a stream language is in a matchingLanguageCodes() set.

list.title: module:streamSelection.isSelectedAudioStreamDirectPlayable
list.description:
isSelectedAudioStreamDirectPlayable: Whether the audio stream at jellyfinAudioIndex inside audioStreams is decodable by the current device.

Used by mid-playback audio switching to decide whether Roku's native track-switch is viable, or whether a server reload is required (e.g. switching back to an 8ch track on a stereo device — Roku can't decode it natively, so a transcode reload is needed).

list.title: module:streamSelection.isStreamDirectPlayable
list.description:
isStreamDirectPlayable: Checks if an audio stream can be directly played by the device

For 8-channel: MUST use PassThru: 1 (only HDMI passthrough, Roku can't decode 8-channel) For 6-channel and below: Use combined check (no PassThru) - checks both Roku and HDMI

list.title: module:streamSelection.mapRokuLocaleToJellyfinLanguage
list.description:
mapRokuLocaleToJellyfinLanguage: Converts Roku locale codes to Jellyfin ISO 639-2 language codes

Maps Roku device locale (e.g., "en_US", "fr_CA") to Jellyfin's 3-letter language codes. Extracts base language from locale and maps to standard ISO 639-2 codes.

Supported Roku locales:

  • en_US, en_GB, en_CA, en_AU → eng (English)
  • es_ES, es_MX → spa (Spanish)
  • pt_BR → por (Portuguese)
  • fr_CA → fra (French)
  • de_DE → deu (German)
  • it_IT → ita (Italian)

list.title: module:streamSelection.matchingLanguageCodes
list.description:
matchingLanguageCodes: The stream language codes that count as a match for a preference.

Exact codes win: when any stream carries the preferred code itself (case-insensitively), only that code matches, so a "pob" preference keeps its Brazilian track over a "por" one. Only when none does are codes for the same language in another form accepted (languagesMatch()) — how a "fre" preference finds a "fra" track, and an OriginalLanguage of "ko" a "kor" one.

Compute it once over ALL the candidate streams, not per filtered subset, so a subset without the exact code cannot fall back to a same-language code the full list would have ruled out.

list.title: module:streamSelection.mediaSourceForId
list.description:
mediaSourceForId: The MediaSource a playback request is for.

mediaSources[0] is only the server's default. A version picked in the Video dropdown sits elsewhere in the list, and from Jellyfin 12.0 the server moves the in-progress version to the front, so anything about the file being PLAYED — its runtime, bitrate, container or streams — has to be read from the source the request names (mediaSourceIndexForId).

are no sources

list.title: module:streamSelection.mediaSourceIndexForId
list.description:
mediaSourceIndexForId: Index of the MediaSource with this id.

Case-insensitive, matching the server: it keys its own per-version lookup with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase and compares source ids with StringComparison .OrdinalIgnoreCase (MediaSourceManager), so it does not assume one spelling of a GUID and neither should any caller that matches one.

list.title: module:streamSelection.needsSeriesOriginalLanguage
list.description: needsSeriesOriginalLanguage: True when an episode's track selection needs its series' OriginalLanguage — the viewer wants the original audio and the episode has none of its own. The server falls back to the series itself (Episode.GetInheritedOriginalLanguage), but sends only the item's own value, and not every metadata provider sets one on episodes. ItemMetaData() fetches it; render-thread callers, which cannot, leave the track to LoadVideoContentTask.

list.title: module:streamSelection.originalAudioStreams
list.description: originalAudioStreams: The streams the file flags as the original audio (MediaStream.IsOriginal).

list.title: module:streamSelection.resolveAudioLanguagePreference
list.description:
resolveAudioLanguagePreference: Resolves the audio language preference setting value

Checks JellyRock override setting first, then falls back to web client setting. Returns a 3-letter ISO 639-2 language code (e.g., "eng", "jpn") or empty string.

The web client's "Original language" choice (12.0+) resolves to the item's OriginalLanguage, which is ISO 639-1 ("ko"), or to "" when the item has none. Pair the result with wantsOriginalAudio(): "" then means "no language rule", not "use the Roku locale".

list.title: module:streamSelection.resolvePlayDefaultAudioTrack
list.description:
resolvePlayDefaultAudioTrack: Resolves the playDefaultAudioTrack setting value

Checks JellyRock override setting first, then falls back to web client setting. Ensures a valid boolean is always returned.

list.title: module:streamSelection.resolveSubtitleLanguagePreference
list.description:
resolveSubtitleLanguagePreference: Resolves the subtitle language preference setting value

Checks JellyRock override setting first, then falls back to web client setting. The "audio" option chains to resolveAudioLanguagePreference() so subtitle language follows the user's audio language override — including "Original language", which follows the item's OriginalLanguage, or applies no language rule when the item has none.

list.title: module:streamSelection.selectAudioStreamIndex
list.description: selectAudioStreamIndex: The audio stream to auto-select for the viewer — their "play default track" and language preferences resolved, then findBestAudioStreamIndex().

list.title: module:streamSelection.selectBestStreamByHardware
list.description:
selectBestStreamByHardware: Selects the best audio stream based on device capabilities

Priority:

  1. Prefer streams matching device's max channel capability (for quality)
  2. Among matching streams, prefer direct-playable codecs
  3. Fall back intelligently based on channel counts

list.title: module:streamSelection.selectSubtitleByMode
list.description: selectSubtitleByMode: Apply subtitle mode selection logic to sorted subtitle entries Mirrors defaultSubtitleTrack() in Subtitles.bs

list.title: module:streamSelection.streamLanguageCodes
list.description: streamLanguageCodes: The Language of each stream of one type, for matchingLanguageCodes().

list.title: module:streamSelection.wantsOriginalAudio
list.description: wantsOriginalAudio: True when the viewer's audio preference is "Original language" — the web client's choice, not overridden by a JellyRock Roku or custom language.

list.title: module:subtitles.defaultSubtitleTrack
list.description: defaultSubtitleTrack:

list.title: module:subtitles.defaultSubtitleTrackFromVid
list.description: defaultSubtitleTrackFromVid: Identifies the default subtitle track given metadata and audio index

list.title: module:subtitles.sortSubtitles
list.description: Checks available subtitle tracks and puts subtitles in forced, default, and non-default/forced but preferred language at the top

list.title: module:tasks.TASK_QUEUE_CAP
list.description: Launches that may wait at once; past it launchTask() refuses. A waiting node costs ~4 KB (measured 2026-09-23 on a 512 MB Streaming Stick 3600X: 3.6-4.1 KB for a LoadItemsTask with small inputs), so the full queue is ~2 MB there. ADR 0041.

list.title: module:tasks.TASK_QUEUE_RETRY_MIN_SECONDS
list.description: How soon the queue first retries its head, and the longest it waits between retries while no slot frees. A refused retry costs render-thread time, and a busy render thread also slows the Tasks the queue waits on, so retries back off while nothing can start. The longest wait is also how late a waiting launch can notice a freed slot. Measured 2026-09-23 on a 512 MB Streaming Stick 3600X at the watermark (TaskLedgerBench drainBlocked): a refused retry costs 2.1 ms reading the ledger only, and cost 2.8 ms when it asked admitTaskLaunch, which also writes it twice.

list.title: module:tasks.TASK_THREAD_WATERMARK
list.description: Live Task threads above which launchTask() queues instead of starting. See the bound above.

list.title: module:tasks.admitTaskLaunch
list.description:
Records node and decides whether its launch may proceed.

Returns false when the app is at or above the watermark, in which case the node is NOT recorded — a launch that has not started holds no thread, so counting it would inflate the ledger on exactly the path that must not spiral. False is not a refusal: launchTask() then queues the node, and the queue's drain asks again once taskLedgerHasRoom says a slot has freed.

list.title: module:tasks.countLiveTaskThreads
list.description:
Counts the tracked nodes whose Task thread is still running.

This is the app's own launches only — it excludes the main and render threads and anything started outside launchTask().

list.title: module:tasks.drainTaskLaunchQueue
list.description:
Starts every waiting launch the ledger now admits, oldest first. Called by TaskLaunchQueue's drain tick. Entries whose node was released while waiting are dropped first (taskQueueDropReleased); the first head the ledger refuses stops the pass, since nothing behind it may jump the order.

A tick with no free slot only reads the ledger. It is the tick that repeats while the app is saturated, and asking admitTaskLaunch would also write the ledger twice.

list.title: module:tasks.enqueueTaskLaunch
list.description: Hands node to the queue; false (a refusal) only when the queue is full.

list.title: module:tasks.isCurrentTaskEvent
list.description: True when event came from current — the run the component still wants. False for an event queued by a node that has since been replaced or released, which the handler must ignore rather than read current in its place.

list.title: module:tasks.isTaskInFlight
list.description: True while node's run is live or waiting in the launch queue. Use it where a caller decides "is my run still going?" — reading state = "run" alone calls a queued run finished, and replacing it sends the new one to the back of the queue.

list.title: module:tasks.launchTask
list.description:
Starts node's Task thread through the accounted chokepoint.

(ADR 0041); false when nothing will start — an invalid node, or a full launch queue. Check it where state depends on the run delivering — a "loading" flag that only the delivery clears must take this result, or a refused launch leaves it set for good. A queued run has not started yet: ask isTaskInFlight(node), not node.state, whether it is still going.

list.title: module:tasks.noteTaskLaunchRefused
list.description: A launch that starts nothing — past the queue's cap, or with no queue yet.

list.title: module:tasks.printTaskThreads
list.description:
Prints the ledger to the BrightScript console (telnet port 8085).

Callable from a paused console the same way as the debug flags: printTaskThreads()

list.title: module:tasks.pruneTaskLedger
list.description:
Returns ledger with finished threads dropped and node recorded.

Pruning at launch (rather than at read) keeps the ledger bounded without depending on anyone calling the readout: it holds the tasks live right now plus any that finished since the previous launch.

node is appended unconditionally and de-duplicated against the existing entries, because a persistent Task node gets relaunched many times over its life (ExtrasRowList alone relaunches its nodes 38 times).

list.title: module:tasks.recordTaskLaunch
list.description:
Records node into store's ledger, creating the field on first use.

The field is CREATED here rather than assumed to exist, because a write to a field an roSGNode does not have is a silent no-op. Measured on device: with the field declared at the end of setGlobalNodes(), the five Task threads that setGlobalNodes() starts before that line — the three ApiTasks, ApiQueueTask and SideEffectTask — were dropped without a trace, and printTaskThreads() under-reported by a permanent five. Creating on first use makes the ledger correct whatever order bootstrap and launches happen in, so the bug cannot come back by someone adding a launch earlier.

store is passed in rather than read from m.global so this stays outside the #if debug shell and a Rooibos test can drive it — test builds compile with debug=false, so anything inside the gate is unreachable from Rooibos.

list.title: module:tasks.releaseTask
list.description:
Stops node's run, if any, and detaches the observer the caller registered on observedField.

Called from the handler of the field the Task writes, it can land before the Task's function returns — the node still reads run there — and a stopped run executes nothing further. So a caller that releases on delivery relies on that field being the Task's LAST write; anything the Task does after it may silently not happen.

list.title: module:tasks.replaceTask
list.description: Releases existing (see releaseTask) and returns a NEW nodeType Task node with fields set, ready to be observed and launched. Always assign the result back: m.task = replaceTask(m.task, "LoadItemsTask", "content", { itemsToLoad: "x" }).

list.title: module:tasks.sharedTaskLedger
list.description: The ledger launchTask() keeps on m.global, or invalid when there is none yet.

list.title: module:tasks.taskLaunchQueue
list.description: The launch queue on m.global, or invalid before setGlobalNodes() has created it.

list.title: module:tasks.taskLedgerHasRoom
list.description: True when ledger has a slot for one more thread: admitTaskLaunch admits a node that holds no thread yet exactly when this is true. Read-only, unlike admitTaskLaunch, so asking costs no ledger write.

list.title: module:tasks.taskQueueAdd
list.description: Adds node to queue (in place) and says what happened: "queued" - appended at the back "already" - it already waits; its entry is re-armed with its current state, so a release-and-relaunch while waiting still starts it once "running" - its thread is live; not queued, just as Roku ignores relaunching a running node "full" - cap entries already wait; not queued

list.title: module:tasks.taskQueueDropReleased
list.description: Returns queue without the entries whose node was released while waiting.

list.title: module:tasks.taskQueueHolds
list.description: True when node waits in queue and has not been released since it was queued.

list.title: module:tasks.taskQueueRetrySeconds
list.description: The wait before the queue's next retry, given the last wait and how many launches the last retry started: back to the shortest once one started (the slots are freeing, so more may follow), otherwise twice the last, up to the longest.

list.title: module:tasks.taskThreadIsLive
list.description:
True while node's Task thread is running.

"init" counts: a node told to RUN has not necessarily entered its function yet, but it is already holding a thread. A node that has never been launched also reports "init", which is why only nodes the ledger has recorded are ever passed here.

list.title: module:textureManager.TEXTURE_BUFFER_ROWS
list.description: Rows kept loaded on each side of the visible rows (see viewport.rowWindow).

list.title: module:textureManager.TEXTURE_BUFFER_THRESHOLD
list.description: Maximum items a row can have before horizontal buffer logic kicks in. Rows at or below this count use renderTracking only — all items stay loaded when on screen because they fit comfortably in texture memory.

list.title: module:textureManager.activateTextureManager
list.description: Activates texture management after initial content load or on onScreenShown. Transitions state from "init" or "hidden" to "active", enabling buffer-based texture management. Callers should update loadedRowRange before calling this.

list.title: module:textureManager.calculateTextureItemSpacing
list.description: Extracts horizontal item spacing from the RowList rowItemSpacing field.

list.title: module:textureManager.calculateTextureVisibleItemCount
list.description: How many item slots of one row are visible at once. A partly visible slot at the right edge counts, because it renders.

list.title: module:textureManager.calculateTextureVisibleWidth
list.description: Calculates the usable row width for determining how many items fit on screen.

list.title: module:textureManager.destroyTextureManager
list.description: Destroys texture management during component teardown. All cells force-unload unconditionally — no guards, no buffer checks.

list.title: module:textureManager.hideTextureManager
list.description: Hides texture management when the screen is no longer visible. Freezes all cells in their current state — textures stay loaded so returning is instant. renderTracking changes are ignored while hidden.

list.title: module:textureManager.initTextureManager
list.description: Adds texture management fields to a RowList content root node. Sets initial state to "init" — cells will not unload during layout changes.

list.title: module:textureManager.isColumnInTextureWindow
list.description:
Whether one column of a long RowList row belongs to the horizontal texture window.

The window keeps TEXTURE_BUFFER_THRESHOLD textures loaded: the visible slots plus the remaining budget split around them, the odd item going to the right. It wraps, because Home's rows use fixedFocusWrap — at column 0 the left half sits at the row's TAIL, which is the item drawn in the focusXOffset gap and one Left press away.

Pure so the geometry can be pinned by unit tests. The column sets those tests assert were read off a Stick 4K with an RTA cell census (32- and 100-item portrait rows), so a change here that moves the window fails a test rather than needing a device to notice.

list.title: module:textureManager.setLoadedRowRange
list.description: Writes range to loadedRowRange only when it differs, so cells observing the field are not woken by a focus move that leaves the window where it was.

list.title: module:textureManager.shouldReloadTexture
list.description:
Decides whether a cell scrolling back into range should re-issue its image load.

THREE paths leave a cell's poster at "" with the real URL still cached, and they do not all want the same thing:

  • unloadTexture() — the manager evicted a resident texture to free memory.
  • deferTextureLoad() — the cell bound while off screen, so no request was ever issued.
  • showPlaceholder() — the image FAILED, and the URI was cleared to reveal the type glyph underneath. The first two want the load; the third does not, because re-requesting a known-broken image wipes the glyph off a cell that is sitting still and then fails again. Deciding on currentUri <> cachedUri cannot separate them — all three look identical from there. isTextureUnloaded can: the first two set it, showPlaceholder does not.

Worth knowing before "fixing" the missing retry: a failed image does NOT retry while its cell stays in range, only at the next unload or rebind. That is deliberate, and the measurement behind it is recorded as failed-poster-no-scroll-retry in docs/decisions.md.

list.title: module:textureManager.updateGridTextureBufferRange
list.description: Calculates and sets the loaded row range for a MarkupGrid based on current focus. Unlike updateTextureBufferRange() which works with hierarchical RowList content (children = rows), this works with flat MarkupGrid content (children = items) and derives row indices from the flat item index and column count.

list.title: module:textureManager.updateTextureBufferRange
list.description: Calculates and sets the loaded row range and focused column based on current focus. The vertical range includes all visible rows plus a 2-row buffer above and below.

list.title: module:trackPickerOptions.availableSubtitleTrackIndex
list.description:
Roku translates the tracks we supply into availableSubtitleTracks, dropping any it does not understand — so its indexing does not match Jellyfin's. This maps a Jellyfin track name onto Roku's list.

Substring rather than equality: Roku mangles the name it was given (our value survives inside it), so an exact compare never matches.

list.title: module:trackPickerOptions.buildAudioTrackOptions
list.description: Audio tracks. values are Jellyfin stream indexes, which is what VideoPlayerView.audioIndex takes.

list.title: module:trackPickerOptions.buildSubtitleTrackOptions
list.description:
Subtitle tracks, with a "None" option always first.

Each value is { index, isEncoded, trackName }: index - Jellyfin stream index, or SubtitleSelection.NONE for the None row isEncoded - burned into the video by the transcoder, so Roku cannot toggle it trackName - the Jellyfin track name, matched against Roku's own mangled availableSubtitleTracks names (see availableSubtitleTrackIndex)

Which row is active depends on where the current subtitle came from: an in-file track is identified by its Jellyfin index, while an external one is only identifiable by matching the Roku track name currently set on the player.

list.title: module:trackPickerOptions.buildVideoSourceOptions
list.description: Video sources (alternate versions of the same item). values are MediaSource ids, which is what VideoPlayerView.mediaSourceId takes.

list.title: module:trackPickerOptions.isSubtitleStreamActive
list.description: Is this the subtitle stream currently showing? Split out because the two cases answer completely different questions (see buildSubtitleTrackOptions).

list.title: module:transcodeCause.TRANSCODE_CAUSE_H264_CEILING_HEIGHT
list.description: The 1080p hardware ceiling ItemPostPlaybackInfo clamps h264 to, independently of any setting. Renamed from TRANSCODE_CAUSE_DEFAULT_MAX_HEIGHT when the resolution predicate stopped treating 1080 as a cap the user could not beat: this is now the ONLY thing 1080 means in this file, and the old name claimed the other one.

list.title: module:transcodeCause.TRANSCODE_CAUSE_STEREO_CAPPED_CODECS
list.description: Codecs whose decode path JellyRock caps at 2 channels when the user turns "Decode Multichannel Audio" off. Mirrors stereoOutputCodecs in deviceCapabilities.bs getCodecProfiles() — and the list is the reason this predicate needs the source CODEC and not just its channel count: an EAC3 5.1 source hitting AudioChannelsNotSupported was not capped by us, because EAC3 is not on this list.

list.title: module:transcodeCause.causedByBitrateLimit
list.description:
Mirrors GetBitRateLimit() in deviceCapabilities.bs — and mirrors it through the SAME mediaNumber coercion, deliberately. That function emits the user's value only when the limit is enabled and the stored value reads as a positive number; otherwise it falls through to Roku's per-codec HARDWARE ceilings, which are not the user's doing and must not be reported as such. If the two ever disagree about what counts as a usable limit, this module would name a setting that did not constrain anything.

The last conjunct — the source actually exceeding the limit — is what turns "the setting is on" into "the setting is why". A 5 Mbps stream under a 20 Mbps cap transcoded for some other reason entirely.

list.title: module:transcodeCause.causedByForceTranscodeAnamorphic
list.description: Mirrors getAnamorphicCondition() in deviceCapabilities.bs, which emits its condition ONLY when this setting is on — so the setting being off means the constraint was never sent and something else produced the reason. The source being anamorphic is the second half: the condition cannot bind on a stream it does not describe.

list.title: module:transcodeCause.causedByMultichannelDecodeOff
list.description:
Mirrors the 2-channel cap in getCodecProfiles() (deviceCapabilities.bs), which applies when playbackDecodeMultichannelAudio is FALSE — note the inversion; the setting reads as "let the Roku decode it", so turning it OFF is what adds a constraint.

The cap only touches TRANSCODE_CAUSE_STEREO_CAPPED_CODECS, so the source codec has to be on that list. This is the predicate most likely to be got wrong by reading the setting name alone: a 5.1 EAC3 source that transcodes for channels was capped by the device's real capabilities, not by this setting.

list.title: module:transcodeCause.causedByPreserveDovi
list.description:
Mirrors the DoVi container-profile injection in ItemPostPlaybackInfo (source/api/items.bs). Every conjunct there is reproduced here, because each one is a way the constraint is NOT injected and therefore a way this reason belongs to someone else:

  • the setting off, or the caller bypassing it on a buffer-overflow retry
  • a device that cannot do DoVi (the injection is skipped entirely)
  • a server below apiVersion 2, where VideoRangeType does not exist
  • a non-mkv container, or an AV1 stream, both explicitly exempted there

list.title: module:transcodeCause.causedByResolutionCap
list.description:
Mirrors getResolutionConditions() in deviceCapabilities.bs, where two of the three branches produce a cap that is NOT the user's choice: "off" -> no conditions at all "auto" -> the device's own height; following the TV is not a choice Any NUMERIC value is the user actively giving something up, and is attributable whenever the source actually exceeds it and the device could have done better.

This used to carry a third exemption — cap >= 1080 -> collapses to the default every device gets — which mirrored a REGRESSION rather than a design. Until jellyrock#866, getResolutionConditions compared the user's height against its own 1080 failure-fallback, so "4k" and "8k" silently became a 1080 cap and there was genuinely nothing to attribute. Now the chosen height is honoured, so a 1080 cap on a 4K device IS the user's doing — auto would have given them 2160 — and staying silent about it would be the false negative this module tries to avoid. The deviceMaxHeight <= cap guard below already expresses "the setting is moot" correctly, which is why removing the exemption needed no replacement for it.

The h264 exclusion is the ambiguity guard. ItemPostPlaybackInfo caps h264 at the 1080p hardware ceiling independently of any setting, so a 4K h264 source would transcode with this setting at its default. Two candidate causes, no way to tell them apart from the reason code, so we claim neither.

list.title: module:transcodeCause.transcodeCauseSettingKey
list.description:
The JellyRock setting that provably caused a transcode reason, as the translationKey of that setting's title.

Returning the setting's OWN title key — the one settings.json already carries — rather than a bespoke phrase is deliberate: the report then names the setting exactly as the Settings screen spells it, which is where the user has to go next. It also means this feature adds one translation string in total instead of a parallel vocabulary that can drift out of sync with the settings UI.

list.title: module:translate.loadChineseLocaleFile
list.description: Load Chinese locale translations with script code layering. Chinese locales use script codes (Hans=Simplified, Hant=Traditional) instead of region codes. Supports 3-layer loading for maximum coverage: zh_Hans: zh.json -> zh_Hans.json (2 layers) zh_Hant: zh.json -> zh_Hant.json (2 layers) zh_Hant_HK: zh.json -> zh_Hant.json -> zh_Hant_HK.json (3 layers)

list.title: module:translate.loadLocaleFile
list.description: Load a locale's translations, layering regional over base when applicable. For regional locales (e.g. "fr_CA"), loads the base language ("fr") first, then overlays regional translations on top. Regional values win on conflicts. For Chinese script codes (e.g. "zh_Hant_HK"), uses 3-layer loading: zh -> zh_Hant -> zh_Hant_HK for maximum translation coverage. For base locales (e.g. "fr"), loads directly.

list.title: module:translate.loadTranslations
list.description: Load translation files for a given locale into m.global. Always loads en_US as fallback. When the active locale IS en_US, both m.global.translations and m.global.translationsFallback reference the same AA (no double memory).

list.title: module:translate.translate
list.description: Translate a key, optionally substituting indexed placeholders {0}, {1}, etc. Falls back to en_US if key is missing from active locale, or returns the key itself if missing from both (makes untranslated strings visible during dev).

list.title: module:translate.translatePlural
list.description: Translate a plural key using zero/one/many suffix convention. Selects the appropriate variant based on count, then delegates to translate().

list.title: module:translateLocale.mapRokuLocaleToTranslationLocale
list.description: Convert Roku's locale format to our standard format. Roku sends underscore format (e.g. "en_US", "fr_CA", "zh_CN"). Most pass through directly since they already match our convention, except Chinese locales which use script codes instead of region codes.

list.title: module:translateLocale.normalizeLocaleCode
list.description: Normalize any locale code to our standard filename convention. Handles input from Jellyfin server, user settings, or any external source. Convention: base languages lowercase (e.g. "fr"), regional variants use underscore with uppercase region (e.g. "fr_CA"), Chinese uses script codes (e.g. "zh_Hans", "zh_Hant", "zh_Hant_HK"), numeric regions stay numeric (e.g. "es_419").

list.title: module:translateLocale.resolveTranslationLocale
list.description: Determine which locale to load using the fallback cascade. Pre-login (isPostLogin=false): global sign-in language -> device locale -> en_US Post-login (isPostLogin=true): user setting -> server language -> device locale -> en_US

list.title: module:url.getBaseUrl
list.description: Extract base URL (scheme + authority) from a full URL

list.title: module:url.getServerBaseUrl
list.description: Extract server base URL by removing a known endpoint path suffix This preserves any base path (e.g., /jellyfin) unlike getBaseUrl() which strips all paths

list.title: module:url.mergePaths
list.description: Merge a relative path with a base path

list.title: module:url.normalizeUrl
list.description:
Normalize a URL for consistent comparison and storage

  • Lowercase scheme
  • Remove default ports (:80 for http, :443 for https)
  • Remove trailing slash from path (except root)
  • Remove empty query strings

list.title: module:url.parseUrlComponents
list.description: Parse URL into components

list.title: module:url.reconstructUrl
list.description: Reconstruct URL from parsed components

list.title: module:url.removeDotSegments
list.description: Remove dot segments from path per RFC 3986 Section 5.2.4

list.title: module:url.resolveUrl
list.description: Resolve a reference URI against a base URI per RFC 3986 Section 5 Note: Only http:// and https:// schemes are supported. Other schemes (mailto:, ftp:, etc.) will be treated as relative paths. The result is automatically normalized (lowercased scheme, default ports removed, trailing slashes stripped, etc.) for consistent comparison and storage.

list.title: module:url.urlsEqual
list.description: Check if two URLs are equivalent after normalization

list.title: module:userAuth.StopRemoteControlReceiver
list.description:
#666/#728: stop the ws:// remote-control receiver AND the socket child it published — ends the listener thread and releases the socket's Task thread. Split out of SignOut so it can be unit tested: SignOut's remaining body writes real (non-test-) registry sections and reaches for the router and the session, none of which a Rooibos suite can stand up, but this block is pure node manipulation. See tests/source/unit/api/stopRemoteControlReceiver.spec.bs.

Parent first (so a receiver still winding down can't spawn a replacement socket), then the published child — STOP kills the receiver mid-loop, so its own closeSocket() teardown never runs. STOP is not a join: the receiver can still be mid-connectAndPump here, so a child created but not yet published to socketNode is missed. That window is bounded, not permanent — the vendored socket loop self-exits once its connection reaches CLOSED.

list.title: module:userAuth.userDataFromAuthResult
list.description:
Turn a Jellyfin AuthenticationResult into the UserData node user.Login() expects, registering the user in available_users on the way.

Shared by the two flows that mint a token — password sign-in (getToken above) and Quick Connect (loginRouter.onQuickConnectAuthenticated). Quick Connect used to build its own node AND then re-fetch the user via AboutMe(); the re-fetch was redundant, because AuthenticationResult.User and GET /Users/{id} return the identical UserDto (diffed against Jellyfin 10.11.11 — same 12 keys, differing only in LastLoginDate / LastActivityDate, neither of which this app reads).

The Quick Connect flow guards the SAME payload one layer up, on the render thread (quickConnectHasSession in source/utils/quickConnect.bs), because this side has nowhere left to report a failure to. The two are deliberate duplicates rather than one shared helper — they sit on opposite threads and answer different questions ("can I build a node?" vs "can I tell the user?") — so if what counts as a usable session ever changes, change both.

list.title: module:videoNotifications.isNotificationVisible
list.description:
Whether a VideoNotification is visually present (including during its fade-out animation). Lives as a free function — not a method on VideoNotification — precisely so it can guard a possibly-invalid reference: callers pass m.segmentNotification / m.nextEpisodeNotification, which can be cleared during player teardown (VideoPlayerView.onDestroy) while an observer such as onPositionChanged still fires. A method (node.callFunc(...)) could not guard its own non-existence and would crash the same way the caller does.

A notification that doesn't exist is, by definition, not visible → false.

list.title: module:webvtt.parseVTT
list.description:
Parses a WebVTT file into caption lines.

A WebVTT file is blocks separated by blank lines, and only a cue's text is shown: the lines after its timing line, up to the next blank line. Everything else — the WEBVTT header, NOTE / STYLE / REGION blocks, and a cue identifier (the optional line BEFORE a timing line) — is skipped, because none of it follows a timing line within its block.

A cue whose timing cannot be read is dropped whole, and its text with it: attaching that text to the previous cue's timing would show it at the wrong moment.

  • start / end in milliseconds; one entry per text line
  • skippedCues counts cues dropped for an unreadable timing line, firstSkipped quotes the first of them

list.title: module:webvtt.vttTimestampPattern
list.description: The timestamp grammar vttTimestampToMs() accepts: [H:]MM:SS.mmm. The hour field is optional in WebVTT. A comma before the milliseconds is not valid WebVTT, but it has reached the app in production (#584), and rejecting it would drop every cue in such a file rather than show them.

list.title: module:webvtt.vttTimestampToMs
list.description:
Milliseconds for one WebVTT timestamp, or -1 when it is not one.

converting many stamps, so the regex is compiled once per file rather than per stamp

list.title: module:webvtt.vttTimingField
list.description: The timestamp at the start of one side of a timing line: the end side can carry cue settings after it (00:28.876 align:start position:10%), and a CRLF file leaves a trailing carriage return.

list.title: nodeHelpers.QueueItem
list.description: Compile-time contract for a queue item AA (the return shape of createQueueItem below). BrighterScript interfaces ARE build-enforced wherever a value is TYPED as the interface (verified on this toolchain: a QueueItem-typed value raises cannot-find-name on an undeclared member and return-type-mismatch on a missing required member). createQueueItem itself returns as object, not as QueueItem — its result is used as a real roAssociativeArray (callers/tests call DoesExist/Count) and an interface return type strips those AA methods (see the return-type note on the function below). So the ENFORCED gate on the returned shape is the createQueueItem spec at tests/source/unit/utils/nodeHelpers.spec.bs; this interface is the single explicit source of truth for the shape, IDE autocomplete, and a build-checked contract for any local you DO type as nodeHelpers.QueueItem. Most members are optional: createQueueItem only copies them when the source carries them, so a bare/lean source yields a minimal item.

list.title: nodeHelpers.createQueueItem
list.description:
createQueueItem: Create a queue item AA from a source item.

The queue item is a thin AA — it carries only what the queue infrastructure and the players need, NOT a full deep copy (that was the original perf win). Video items stay minimal: LoadVideoContentTask re-fetches all metadata server-side via ItemMetaData() on mount. AUDIO is different — the audio player advances IN PLACE and AudioPlayerView renders the now-playing text/poster directly off the queue item, so the display fields (name/artists/albumArtist/ albumName/albumId/image tags) MUST be carried; without them every track change paid a redundant per-track metadata fetch whose latency popped the artist/album in late.

Accepts either a JellyfinBaseItem node (typed camelCase fields) or a raw Jellyfin API response AA (PascalCase fields). BrightScript AA lookup is case-insensitive, so field access works identically for both — e.g. sourceNode.backdropImageTags finds BackdropImageTags on a raw API AA and backdropImageTags on a typed node.

Fields always present in the returned AA (guaranteed contract):

  • backdropImageTags: Array of backdrop image tags (empty array = no backdrop)
  • parentBackdropImageTags: Array of parent backdrop tags (empty array = none)
  • parentBackdropItemId: Parent item ID for parent backdrops (empty string = none)

Fields present only when non-empty / non-zero:

  • id: Item identifier (required for playback)
  • type: Media type (required for queue routing)
  • title: Display title
  • mediaSourceId: Media source hint
  • runTimeTicks: Runtime duration
  • name / artists / albumArtist / albumName / albumId / albumPrimaryImageTag / primaryImageTag: now-playing display fields (audio plays in place — see header)
  • seriesId: Series ID for episode navigation in resume dialog
  • seasonId: Season ID for episode navigation in resume dialog
  • playbackPositionTicks: Saved resume position

Callers set selectedAudioStreamIndex on the returned AA after creation, and the start position through setResumeStart() or setExactStart().

Returns object, not QueueItem: the queue item is used as a real roAssociativeArray (callers/tests use DoesExist/Count), and typing it as the interface would strip those AA methods. The QueueItem interface is the documented, opt-in shape (type a local as nodeHelpers.QueueItem for autocomplete); the createQueueItem spec is the enforced gate.

list.title: nodeHelpers.setExactStart
list.description: setExactStart: Start a queue item at a place the caller named — a chapter, Play from the start, the position a reload saved. The loader never replaces it.

list.title: nodeHelpers.setResumeStart
list.description:
setResumeStart: Start a queue item from its saved resume position.

The loader may replace it: on a per-version server it chooses which version resumes and starts that version at ITS OWN position, which the caller could not read.

list.title: nodeHelpers.startFresh
list.description: startFresh: Start a queue item from the beginning because the viewer did not choose to resume it (QueueManager.advanceTo / startCurrentFresh). An exact start at 0, so the loader never swaps in a version's saved position; startsFresh, so it picks the version by the viewer's explicit pick instead; and no version counts as in progress, since none resumes.

list.title: nodeUtils.populateNodeFromAA
list.description:
Populate a ContentNode from an associative array

Example: localServer = m.global.server mockData = MockDataLoader.LoadServer("default") nodeUtils.populateNodeFromAA(localServer, mockData, [])

IMPORTANT: When populating nodes on m.global, get a local reference first This minimizes rendezvous

list.title: nodeUtils.populateNodeFromNode
list.description:
Populate a ContentNode from another ContentNode's fields

Example: localServer = m.global.server transformedServer = transformer.transformServerInfo(mockData) nodeUtils.populateNodeFromNode(localServer, transformedServer, [])

IMPORTANT: When populating nodes on m.global, get a local reference first This minimizes rendezvous

list.title: nodeUtils.resetNodeToDefaults
list.description:
Reset a ContentNode to its XML-defined defaults

Example: localServer = m.global.server nodeUtils.resetNodeToDefaults(localServer, "JellyfinServer", [])

IMPORTANT: When resetting nodes on m.global, get a local reference first This minimizes rendezvous (only 1 rendezvous to get local ref, then 0 for reset)

list.title: paging
list.description:
Paging a query across Task runs: what each page asks for, and whether another page follows.

A paged load runs every page on a NEW Task node (see replaceTask in tasks.bs), so the node cannot be the memory of the query: each page must ask for exactly what the first page asked for. The screen holds the query as a plain AA and hands each run a copy with that page's startIndex. BaseGridView and the TV guide (Schedule) both page this way.

list.title: paging.forPage
list.description: The fields for one run of query, starting at startIndex. A copy: query itself is left untouched, so it stays the record of what every page of the load asks for.

list.title: paging.nextStart
list.description:
Where the next page starts, or -1 when the load is complete.

A page that delivers nothing ends the load even when total says more exist: the next request would ask for the same startIndex and get the same empty answer, forever.

list.title: quickplay
list.description: Render-thread-safe Quick Play helpers. API-calling quickplay logic lives in QuickPlayTask (components/tasks/QuickPlayTask.bs).

list.title: quickplay.audio

list.title: quickplay.musicVideo
list.description: A single music video file.
